dervis-irab:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(حم. وَالْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ) حم: what has been said about the openings of the surahs, in meaning and in i'rab, has already preceded. The waw is the waw of oath. «الكتاب» is genitive by the waw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (أقسم). «المبين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الكتاب». (إِنَّا جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ) «إن» and its noun, and the clause «جعلناه» is its khabar (predicate). «جعلناه», that is, "we made it" (صيّرناه), is a verb, agent and direct object; «قرآنا» is a second direct object; «عربيا» is an adjective; «لعل» and its noun, and the clause «تعقلون» is its khabar. The clause «إنّا جعلناه» is the jawāb al-qasam (answer to the oath), and this answer has captivated the scholars of rhetoric, as will come later. Al-Zamakhsharī permitted «جعلناه» to mean "we created it" (خلقناه), following the principle of the Muʿtazila in holding that the Qur'an is created; a discussion of this will come in the section on Benefits. On that reading «قرآنا» would be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, and the clause «لعلكم تعقلون» would be causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position, because hope (tarajjī) is borrowed here for the meaning of intention, i.e. "We made it an Arabic Qur'an intending that the Arabs should understand it." (وَإِنَّهُ فِي أُمِّ الْكِتابِ لَدَيْنا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ) The waw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the answer of the oath, so it is in effect a second answer. «إن» and its noun; «في أم الكتاب» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar, the implied form being "established" (مثبت). «أم الكتاب» is the origin of the books, that is, the Preserved Tablet. He the Exalted said: «بل هو قرآن مجيد في لوح محفوظ» ("Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an, on a Preserved Tablet"). «ولدينا» is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl. The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «علي» is a second khabar and «حكيم» a third khabar. Some have objected to this i'rab because it puts a khabar not accompanied by the lām before one accompanied by it. Abu al-Baqāʾ said: "«في أم الكتاب» is attached to «علي», and the lām does not prevent that; «ولدينا» is a badal (substitute) for the preposition and its genitive noun. It may also be a ḥāl from «الكتاب» or from «أم». Neither of the two adverbials may be the khabar, because the khabar must of necessity be «علي» on account of the lām; but each of them may be an adjective of the khabar, which then became a ḥāl by being placed before it." (أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكُمُ الذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً أَنْ كُنْتُمْ قَوْماً مُسْرِفِينَ) The hamza is for rhetorical (disapproving) interrogation. The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted element implied between it and the hamza, its implied form being "Shall we neglect you, and so turn away…?" «نضرب» is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we" (نحن). «عنكم» is attached to «نضرب»; «الذكر» is a direct object, meaning the Qur'an. In «صفحا» there are several possible analyses. First, that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) synonymous in meaning with «نضرب», since one says "ḍaraba ʿan such-and-such" and "aḍraba ʿanhu" meaning he turned away from it and turned his face from it. Second, that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «نضرب», i.e. "pardoning/turning away" (صافحين). Third, that it is accusative as an adverbial meaning "side", from their saying "he looked at him sideways (bi-ṣafḥ wajhihi)", as you say "put this book aside" and "walk aside". Fourth, that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the meaning being: "Shall we withhold from you the sending down of the Qur'an and the imposition of the proof by it, out of turning away from you?" More will be said on this verse. «أن» is a maṣdar particle; it has also been read with kasra on the hamza («إن»), in which case it is conditional. On the first reading, it and what follows it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; on the second, «كنتم» is the protasis and the apodosis is omitted. The words of al-Zamakhsharī: "If you say: how can the meaning of the conditional «إن» be sound when they were in fact transgressors beyond doubt? I say: it belongs to the kind of condition that I mentioned, which issues from one who is confident (al-mudill) of the soundness of a matter that is certain because it is established, as the hired worker says: 'If I have worked for you, then pay me my due,' while he knows that he has. But he makes it appear in his speech that your negligence in departing from the truth is the act of one in doubt about the entitlement despite its clarity, treating him as ignorant." «كنتم»: kāna and its noun, «قوما» is its khabar, and «مسرفين» is an adjective. (وَكَمْ أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ نَبِيٍّ فِي الْأَوَّلِينَ) «كم» is khabariyya (exclamatory, "how many") in the position of accusative, a preposed direct object of «أرسلنا»; «من نبي» is a tamyīz (specification) of the khabariyya «كم»; «في الأولين» is attached to «أرسلنا». (وَما يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ إِلَّا كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) The waw is a conjunction, «ما» is negative, «يأتيهم» is an imperfect verb in the nominative with a preposed direct object; «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and «نبي» is genitive in form and nominative in position as the agent; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «كان» and its noun; «به» is attached to «يستهزئون», and the clause «يستهزئون» is the khabar of «كانوا». (فَأَهْلَكْنا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشاً وَمَضى مَثَلُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) The fāʾ is the "eloquent fāʾ" (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa). «أهلكنا» is verb and agent; «أشد» is a direct object; «منهم» is attached to «أشد»; «بطشا» is a tamyīz according to the more likely view, and it has been said to be a ḥāl from the agent of «أهلكنا», i.e. "while striking" (باطشين), but I regard that as sheer affectation. «ومضى» is conjoined to «فأهلكنا», and «مثل الأولين» is the agent of «مضى».

* Rhetoric:
1- The oath in His words «والكتاب المبين إنّا جعلناه» (the verse) is the art of congruity (fann al-tanāsub). He swore by the Qur'an, and one swears only by something great; then He made the matter sworn upon the magnification of the Qur'an, in that it is an Arabic Qur'an which it is hoped the worlds may use to understand. Thus the answer to the oath validated the oath, and congruity was completed between the oath and that sworn by, since both are from one valley. The poets have clung to the hems of this lofty rhetorical device, and Abu Tammām swore by the front teeth when he said:
وثناياك إنها إغريض ... ولآل توم وبرق وميض
وأقاح منوّر في بطاح ... هزّه في الصباح روض أريض
وارتكاض الكرى بعينيك في النوم فنونا وما لعيني غموض
(By your front teeth, they are ighrīḍ, and pearls, and a flashing lightning; and chamomile in bloom in the lowlands, stirred at dawn by a fertile meadow; and the stirring of sleep in your eyes in slumber, in many ways, while my eyes have no sleep.) [Translator's note: the Arabic text of the third verse as printed in the source reads «ارتكاض الكرى بعينيك في النوم فنونا»; the source's line division splits «بعيني / ك»; I have rendered it as one word.]
Abu Tammām swore by the front teeth, which are the front of the teeth, that they are ighrīḍ; so the oath and its answer relate to one thing. The ighrīḍ, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, is the spathe of the palm (al-ṭalʿ) and anything white and fresh; and al-tūm, singular tūma, is a bead made of silver like a pearl.
2- Metaphor (istiʿāra): in His words «وإنه في أم الكتاب» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya). The word "mother" (umm) has been borrowed for "origin" (aṣl), which is the omitted tenor (mushabbah), because children arise from the mother as branches arise from roots. The wisdom in this is to depict what is not seen so that it becomes seen; but this metaphor adds nothing except manifestness, because the mother is more manifest to the senses than the origin.

* Benefits:
1- The trial of the creation of the Qur'an: the Muʿtazila held the denial of the attributes of meaning (ṣifāt al-maʿānī) of Allah the Exalted, among them speech, because affirming them leads to anthropomorphism (tashbīh) and to a multiplicity of eternal things, which contradicts tawḥīd (divine oneness). One of the necessary consequences was that they said that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, created. The author of al-Mawāqif said: "The Muʿtazila said: His speech, the Exalted, is sounds and letters, but they do not subsist in His essence; rather Allah creates them in something other than Him, such as the Preserved Tablet, or Jibrīl, or the Prophet, and it is originated." The Muʿtazila were not the first to say the Qur'an was created, just as they were not the first to deny the attributes. Rather the first known to have said it was created was al-Jaʿd ibn Dirham in Damascus, who was the tutor of Marwān ibn Muḥammad, the last of the caliphs of the Umayyads, and from him Jahm ibn Ṣafwān al-Tirmidhī, leader of the determinist sect the Jahmiyya, took that doctrine and said it was created, since the Jahmiyya deny the attributes. They also mention that Bishr ibn Ghiyāth al-Marīsī, leader of the Marīsiyya, one of the sects of the Murjiʾa, also said the Qur'an was created in the age of al-Rashīd. Abū Yūsuf forbade him from that, but he did not desist, so he shunned him and expelled him from his gathering, saying: "He will not stop until he spoils a piece of wood" (meaning crucifixion). When that reached al-Rashīd he said: "I vow that if Allah gives me victory over him I will kill him." Bishr remained in hiding throughout al-Rashīd's caliphate and was not caught despite the intensity of the search for him. They also mention that Ḥafṣ al-Fard, one of the greatest of the determinists (al-mujbira), held that doctrine and that al-Shāfiʿī debated him and declared him an unbeliever. In the age of al-Rashīd people were divided on that question between accepting and rejecting, until al-Maʾmūn took office and held that it was created; he was among the fiercest supporters of Iʿtizāl. It would take long to relate the course of this trial, so refer to it in its many sources if you wish.
However, we do not pass over this topic without pointing to the ordeal of Imam Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, because of its fame. We say: al-Muʿtaṣim brought Imam Aḥmad and convened a debating session for him, in which were ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, the judge Aḥmad ibn Abī Duʾād and others. They debated him for three days and he did not cease disputing with them until the fourth day, when al-Muʿtaṣim ordered him flogged with whips. He did not turn from his opinion until he fainted; ʿUjayf ibn ʿAnbasa prodded him with a sword, a mat (bāriya, which is the woven rush mat) was thrown over him and he was trampled upon; then he was carried to his house after being struck thirty-eight lashes. The length of his imprisonment was twenty-eight months. Refer to Tārīkh al-Ṭabarī, Wafayāt al-Aʿyān and Murūj al-Dhahab to read the astonishing reports of this trial.
2- We promised you that we would speak to you about the style of the Qur'an, so we say:
The Qur'an contains many words which some of the Companions and the Followers described as not being of the language of the Arabs, and scholars have written special books on this. The presence of loanwords (muʿarrab) in the Qur'an is a scholarly question on which scholars differed greatly, in two opinions, one of which:
The first opinion: the presence of loanwords in the Qur'an. To this went some of the Companions, the Followers and the scholars, among them Ibn ʿAbbās, Wahb ibn Munabbih, Ibn Masʿūd, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Suddī, Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, ʿAmr ibn Sharaḥbīl, Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn al-Ḥājib, al-Suyūṭī and others.
The second opinion: that the Qur'an contains no non-Arabic words, which is the doctrine of many scholars, among them Imam al-Shāfiʿī, Abū ʿUbayda, Ibn Fāris, Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, al-Bāqillānī, al-Rāzī and others.
It is not very useful to present the details of both opinions, their proofs and the rebuttals of them; what is useful here is to understand the following matters:
1- Later students have accepted the following report from Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām, as if finding in it a solution to the question and an exit from this disagreement. The report is: Abū ʿUbayd said: "It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and others, concerning many words, that they are not of the tongue of the Arabs, such as (سجيل and المشكاة and اليم and الطور and أباريق and استبرق) and the like. These men know interpretation better than Abū ʿUbayda, but they took one position and he took another, and both are correct, Allah willing.
That is because these words are originally not of the tongue of the Arabs; so those men spoke according to the origin, then the Arabs pronounced them with their tongues and Arabized them, so they became Arabic through that; thus they are Arabic in this state, non-Arabic in origin. This statement therefore holds true of both groups."
Al-Jawālīqī cited this report after citing the words of Abū ʿUbayda: "Whoever claims that there is in the Qur'an a tongue other than Arabic has made a grave claim against Allah," and he argued with His words: «إنّا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون». Then this report was transmitted by those who came after al-Jawālīqī and studied the subject of Arabization in the Qur'an, such as al-Suyūṭī and others.
2- Whether the words occurring in the Qur'an from other languages are non-Arabic in origin and Arabic in present state, or non-Arabic in both origin and state, their occurrence in the Qur'an shows that the Arabs understood and accepted them, and their understanding of them shows that they were widespread among them before it came to them; and this proves what we are concerned with, namely the existence of words borrowed from other languages in the Jāhiliyya and the continuation of that when Islam came.
3- It appears that those who rejected the existence of loanwords in the Qur'an were dominated by religious restraint more than by determination of the linguistic reality. Hence, when al-Suyūṭī cited these words in his two books «al-Mutawakkilī fīmā fī al-Qur'ān min al-Muʿarrab» and «al-Muhadhdhab fīmā waqaʿa fī al-Qur'ān min al-Muʿarrab», he set before them chains of transmission attributing them to the Companions and Followers, as though he too were guarding himself against asserting it on his own. He enumerated the languages from which those words were taken and brought them to ten, namely: Abyssinian, Persian, Greek (Rūmiyya), Indian, Syriac, Hebrew, Nabataean, Coptic, Turkish, Zanji and Berber. [Translator's note: the source says "ten" but lists eleven languages.]

dervis-irab:46-56.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain an objection that Pharaoh raised against Moses, just as Quraysh raised the objection of poverty against Muhammad ﷺ. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of affirmation; أرسلنا is a verb and agent; موسى is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi); بآياتنا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), the bāʾ being the bāʾ of accompaniment; إلى فرعون are both attached (mutaʿalliq) to أرسلنا; and ملئه is conjoined to فرعون. (فَقالَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إني is inna and its noun; رسول رب العالمين is its predicate (khabar); and the clause of inna and what follows it is the content of what was said. (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ بِآياتِنا إِذا هُمْ مِنْها يَضْحَكُونَ) The fāʾ is conjoined to something implied, that is, "so they asked him for signs proving his truthfulness"; لما is a temporal adverbial or a connective; جاءهم is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; بآياتنا are both attached to جاءهم; and إذا is the particle of surprise. You may take it as an adverbial governed by the verb of surprise which is the apodosis of لما, and you may take it as a particle. What follows is the text of Abū Ḥayyān's statement on this matter. He said: «Al-Zamakhsharī said: If you ask, how is it permissible for لما to be answered by the إذا of surprise? I say: because the verb of surprise is implied with it, and it is what governs the accusative in its position, as if it were said: "when he came to them with Our signs, they were surprised and laughed". End of quotation. We know of no grammarian who held what this man held, namely that the إذا of surprise is put in the accusative by an implied verb whose implied form is "he surprised"; rather the views about it are three: either it is a particle, and so needs no governor; or an adverb of place; or an adverb of time. If a predicate of kāna is mentioned after the noun that follows it, it is accusative as an adverbial, and the governor in it is that predicate, as in خرجت فإذا زيد قائم, whose implied form is "I went out, and in the place where I went out Zayd was standing" or "and at the time I went out Zayd was standing". If nothing is mentioned after the noun, or an accusative noun is mentioned as a ḥāl, then إذا is the predicate of the subject (mubtadaʾ). If the noun is a body, and we say it is an adverb of place, the matter is clear, as in خرجت فإذا الأسد, that is, "and in the presence was the lion", or فإذا الأسد رابضا ("and there was the lion, crouching"). If we say it is an adverb of time, then there is an omitted muḍāf (the first term of a genitive construct), so that time is not predicated of a body, as in خرجت فإذا الأسد, that is, "and at the time was the lion's presence". As for what al-Zamakhsharī claims, the implying of a verb of surprise, it has not been uttered, not even in a single place. Then the surprise he claims is not indicated by the meaning as coming from the preceding speech; rather the meaning indicates that the surprise comes from the speech in which إذا occurs. You say خرجت فإذا الأسد and the meaning is "and the lion surprised me", not "and I surprised the lion".» We have already given the discussion of the إذا of surprise. هم is a subject (mubtadaʾ); منها are both attached to يضحكون; and the clause يضحكون is their predicate. (وَما نُرِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ إِلَّا هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِها) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; نريهم is a verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; من is a redundant preposition; آية is the second direct object of نريهم; إلا is a particle of restriction; هي is a subject; أكبر is the predicate; من أختها are both attached to أكبر; and the clause is an adjective of آية. More discussion of this saying will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (وَأَخَذْناهُمْ بِالْعَذابِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; أخذناهم is a verb, an agent and a direct object; بالعذاب are both attached to أخذناهم; and لعل with its noun and its predicate. (وَقالُوا: يا أَيُّهَا السَّاحِرُ ادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ بِما عَهِدَ عِنْدَكَ إِنَّنا لَمُهْتَدُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and an agent; يا أيها is a vocative, whose i'rab has already been given; الساحر is a substitute (badal) for أي or an adjective of it; ادع is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the weak letter; لنا are both attached to ادع; ربك is a direct object; بما are both attached to ادع; ما may be a relative noun or a maṣdar (verbal-noun) particle, and the clause عهد is a ṣila (relative clause) or is interpreted as a maṣdar in the genitive by the bāʾ; عندك is an adverbial attached to عهد; and إن with its noun, and لمهتدون is its predicate, with the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). (فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنا عَنْهُمُ الْعَذابَ إِذا هُمْ يَنْكُثُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied element, that is, "so Moses prayed, and when We removed"; لما is a connective or temporal; كشفنا is a verb and an agent; عنهم are both attached to كشفنا; العذاب is a direct object; إذا is the particle of surprise, which has been discussed in detail; هم is a subject; and the clause ينكثون is its predicate. (وَنادى فِرْعَوْنُ فِي قَوْمِهِ قالَ يا قَوْمِ أَلَيْسَ لِي مُلْكُ مِصْرَ وَهذِهِ الْأَنْهارُ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِي أَفَلا تُبْصِرُونَ) The wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; نادى فرعون is a verb and an agent; في قومه are both attached to نادى (the secret of this calling and of the containment will come in the chapter on rhetoric); قال is a past verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "he", and the clause is explicative; يا قوم is a vocative, a muḍāf to the omitted first-person yāʾ.
The hamza is for confirmatory interrogation; ليس is a defective, inert past verb; لي is its fronted predicate; and ملك مصر is its postponed noun. This wāw is either circumstantial, in which case the clause is in the accusative as a ḥāl, or a conjunction, in which case هذه is conjoined to ملك مصر; on the first view هذه is a subject, الأنهار is a substitute, the clause تجري is the predicate, and من تحتي are both attached to تجري. أفلا: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied element, لا is negative, and تبصرون is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn. (أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْ هذَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ) أم is a conjunction; it is munqaṭiʿa (disjunctive), taken to mean بل together with the hamza, that is, "rather, I am better"; so it is disjunctive in expression but connected (muttaṣila) in meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Suyūṭī said: this أم is connected, because the meaning is "Do you not see, or do you see?", except that he put the words "I am better" in the place of "you see", because if they said to him "You are better", they would be seeing people in his view; and this is a case of setting the cause in the place of the effect. Abū Ḥayyān objected to al-Zamakhsharī that the correlate (muʿādil) is not omitted after أم unless the word لا follows it, as in أتقول أم لا, that is, "or do you not say?"; as for omitting it without لا, as here, it is not permitted, although the omission of أم and the correlate has occurred, though rarely, and among it is the poet's verse:
دعاني إليها القلب إني لأمره ... سميع فما أدري أرشد طلابها
(The heart called me to her; I am obedient to its command, so I do not know whether seeking her is right.) He means "or error".
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «أم here is disjunctive in expression because a sentence occurs after it, and in meaning it is connected and correlative, since the meaning is "I am better than him, or not".» More of this discussion will come in the section on benefits. أنا is a subject; خير is the predicate; من هذا are both attached to خير; الذي is a substitute for the demonstrative; هو is a subject; مهين is the predicate; and the clause is the ṣila of الذي. (وَلا يَكادُ يُبِينُ) You may take the wāw as a conjunction, so that the clause is conjoined to the ṣila of the relative noun; you may take it as resumptive, so that the clause also has no grammatical position; and they permitted that it be circumstantial. لا is negative; يكاد is a defective imperfect verb, one of the verbs of approximation (afʿāl al-muqāraba); its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; and the clause يبين is the predicate of يكاد, that is, "make his speech clear". (فَلَوْلا أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لولا is a particle of urging, meaning هلّا ("why not"); ألقي is a passive past verb; عليه are both attached to ألقي; أسورة is a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil), the plural of سوار ("bracelet"); and من ذهب is an adjective of أسورة. (أَوْ جاءَ مَعَهُ الْمَلائِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ)
أو is a conjunction; جاء is a past verb; معه is an adverbial attached to جاء; الملائكة is the agent; and مقترنين is a ḥāl, that is, "following one another, testifying to his truthfulness". (فَاسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ فَأَطاعُوهُ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; استخف is a past verb, meaning "he incited", and in al-Mukhtār: «استفزه الخوف: استخفه» ("fear incited him: it made him light"), and in al-Miṣbāḥ: «واستخف قومه: حملهم على الخفّة والجهل» ("he made his people light: he drove them to levity and ignorance"); قومه is a direct object. فأطاعوه: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أطاعوه is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; إن with its noun; the clause كانوا is its predicate; the clause of inna is causal and has no grammatical position; قوما is the predicate of كانوا; and فاسقين is an adjective. (فَلَمَّا آسَفُونا انْتَقَمْنا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْناهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal, adverbial, or a connective; آسفونا is a past verb, an agent and a direct object, derived by the hamza from أسف when he is angry, so it made it transitive by the hamza; the meaning is "when they did what warrants the exercise of forbearance and rouses indignation". The clause انتقمنا has no grammatical position because it is the answer to لما; منهم are both attached to انتقمنا; فأغرقناهم is conjoined to انتقمنا; and أجمعين is an emphasis (tawkīd) for the hāʾ. (فَجَعَلْناهُمْ سَلَفاً وَمَثَلًا لِلْآخِرِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; جعلناهم is a verb, an agent and a first direct object; سلفا is the second direct object, that is, "predecessors, going ahead to the punishment so that others may take a lesson from them"; مثلا is conjoined to سلفا; and للآخرين is an adjective of مثلا.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «وما نريهم من آية إلا هي أكبر من أختها» there is a comprehensive and exclusive statement, meaning that they are described as great, hardly differing in it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Such is the custom with things that meet in excellence and whose ranks differ in it by only a slight difference: people's opinions differ over which is better, so some prefer this one and some that one. On this people built their speech, saying: "Have you seen men, some of whom are better than others?" Sometimes the opinions of a single man differ about them, so at one time he prefers this one and at another that one. To it belongs the verse from the Ḥamāsa:
من تلق منهم تقل لاقيت سيدهم ... مثل النجوم التي يسري بها الساري
(Whomever of them you meet you say, "I have met their chief", like the stars by which the night traveller is guided.)
The woman of Anmār compared one of her sons with another, then, when she saw their ranks close together with little difference, said: "May they be bereaved of me, if I know which of them is better! They are like a ring of metal, in which one does not know where its two ends are."» So the description by "greatness" is figurative (majāz), and it is relative to those who look at them.
2- Figurative language also: in His saying «ونادى فرعون في قومه» there is a majāz mursal (loose metonymy) whose relation is locality, for he made his people the place of his calling and its site. The meaning is that he commanded the calling in their gatherings and places, just as what is meant by "he called among them" is that the calling is attributed to him, like your saying "the emir cut off the thief" when he commanded that he be cut off.

* Benefits:
أم also: We presented in the chapter on i'rab a glimpse of أم and mentioned in earlier places of this book weighty discussions about it. Here we quote the delightful chapter that the author of al-Mughnī devoted to it, with a useful comment on it. Ibn Hishām said: «The omission of the connected أم and of what is conjoined to it has been heard, as in the saying of the Hudhalī: دعاني أيها القلب إني لأمره ... سميع فما أدري أرشد طلابها
(The heart called me; I am obedient to its command, so I do not know whether seeking her is right.)
Its implied form is "or error". So they said, and there is a discussion of it, as already mentioned (that is, in the section on the single alif, that the hamza here is like هل and so needs no correlate). Some permitted the omission of what is conjoined to it without it, and said, regarding the saying of the Exalted «أفلا تبصرون أم», that the pause is here and that the implied form is "or do you see?", then he begins "I am better". This is false, since the omission of a conjoined element without its conjunction has never been heard; the conjoined element is rather the sentence "I am better". The aspect of equivalence between it and the preceding sentence is that the original is "or do you see?", then the nominal sentence was set in the place of the verbal one, and the cause in the place of the effect, because if they said to him "You are better", they would be seeing people in his view; and this is the meaning of Sībawayh's speech. If you ask: they say أتفعل هذا أم لا, and the original is "or you do not do it?", I say: the omission occurred only after لا and did not occur after the conjunction; and the particles of response often have sentences omitted after them and stand in expression in the place of those sentences, so it is as though the sentence were mentioned here owing to the presence of what makes it unnecessary.»
Sībawayh's wording in al-Kitāb: «This is the chapter of the disjunctive أم, and it is your saying: أعمرو عندك أم عندك زيد. This is not on a par with أيّهما عندك ("which of them is with you?"); do you not see that if you said أيّهما عندك it would not be sound except by repetition and emphasis? What shows you that the latter is cut off from the former is the man's saying "It is a camel", then saying "or a sheep"; so just as أم comes here after a statement, disjunctive, so it comes after an interrogative. That is because when he said أعمرو عندك he supposed that he was with him, then a like supposition overtook him about Zayd after his speech had been completed. Then he said: and like that: وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي أفلا تبصرون أم أنا خير, as if Pharaoh had said "Do you not see, or are you seeing?" So his saying "or am I better" is on a par with "or are you seeing", because had they said "You are better than he", it would have been on a par with their saying "We are seeing". So likewise "or am I better" is on a par with "or are you seeing".» Sībawayh thus ruled that أم is disjunctive.

dervis-irab:57-62.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا إِذا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain another kind of their obstinacy and persistence in stubborn arrogance. لما is temporal or a connective; ضرب is a passive past verb; ابن مريم is a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); and مثلا is a second direct object, because ضرب has been given the sense of جعل ("made"); it may also be parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "he was mentioned as an example". إذا is the particle of surprise, discussed above; قومك is a subject (mubtadaʾ); منه are both attached to يصدون; and the clause يصدون is the predicate of قومك. It is read with kasra on the ṣād, that is, a clamour and uproar rose from them out of joy, delight and laughter at what they heard (the story will come in the section on benefits). It was also read يصدون with ḍamma, from ṣudūd, meaning turning away; and it is said that they are two dialects. (وَقالُوا أَآلِهَتُنا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هُوَ) The wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and an agent; the hamza is for interrogation; آلهتنا is a subject; خير is the predicate; أم is a conjunction and is connected (muttaṣila); and هو is conjoined to آلهتنا. (ما ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلًا بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ خَصِمُونَ) ما is negative; ضربوه is a verb, an agent and a direct object; لك are both attached to ضربوه; إلا is a particle of restriction; جدلا is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), that is, for the sake of disputation, wrangling and obstinacy, not to show the truth; it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl, that is, "not disputing"; بل is a particle of rectification; هم is a subject; قوم is the predicate; and خصمون is an adjective of قوم. (إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا عَبْدٌ أَنْعَمْنا عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلْناهُ مَثَلًا لِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) إن is negative; هو is a subject; إلا is a particle of restriction; عبد is the predicate of هو; the clause أنعمنا is an adjective of عبد; عليه are both attached to أنعمنا; جعلناه is conjoined to أنعمنا; مثلا is the second direct object of جعلناه; and لبني إسرائيل is an adjective of مثلا. (وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَجَعَلْنا مِنْكُمْ مَلائِكَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ يَخْلُفُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; لو is conditional; نشاء is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its agent latent, its implied form being "We"; the lām occurs in the answer of لولا «[Translator's note: the source reads «لولا» where «لو» is evidently meant]»; جعلنا is a verb and an agent; منكم is in the position of the second direct object if جعلنا means "We made", and if it means "We created", the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعلنا; في الأرض are both attached to يخلفون; and the clause يخلفون is an adjective of ملائكة. Some grammarians said: «من is for substitution, that is, "We would have made angels in your place", and they counted among that the saying of the Exalted «أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة», that is, in place of the hereafter, and the poet's verse:
أخذوا المخاض من الفصيل غلبة ... ظلما ويكتب للأمير أقالا
(They took the pregnant she-camels in place of the weanling by force, unjustly, and "more" is written for the emir.)
that is, in place of the weanling. But it is better that it is partitive, as we mentioned in the i'rab.» «[Translator's note: the source reads «في الإعراض» (in the turning away) where «في الإعراب» (in the i'rab) is evidently meant, and the opening quotation mark before «من تكون للبدل» is never closed in the source.]» (وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِلسَّاعَةِ فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِها) The wāw is a conjunction; إن with its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); علم is the predicate of إنه; and للساعة is an adjective of علم, that is, a condition (sharṭ) among its portents by which it is known, so the portent was named "knowledge" because knowledge is obtained through it. The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent inference (al-faṣīḥa); لا is prohibitive; تمترن is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent; and the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis. المرية means doubt. (وَاتَّبِعُونِ هذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; اتبعوني is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; the nūn is the protective nūn; the yāʾ, omitted in writing to follow the practice of the codex, is a direct object; هذا is a subject; صراط is the predicate; and مستقيم is an adjective. (وَلا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطانُ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; يصدنكم is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of the jussive by لا; the kāf is a direct object; الشيطان is the agent; and the clause إنه لكم عدو مبين is causal and has no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
Among the delightful stories that historians relate concerning this verse «ولما ضرب ابن مريم مثلا إذا قومك منه يصدّون»: they mention that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to Quraysh «إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم» ("you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell"), they were intensely resentful of that, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā said: "O Muḥammad, is this for us and our gods in particular, or for all the nations?" He, peace be upon him, said: "It is for you and for all the nations." He said: "By the Lord of the Kaʿba, I have bested you! Do the Christians not worship the Messiah, and the Jews worship ʿUzayr, and the Banū Mulayḥ worship the angels? If these are in the Fire, then we are content that we and our gods be with them." So they rejoiced and laughed and their voices rose, and that is the saying of the Exalted: «إذا قومك منه يصدون». Allah refuted their stubbornness, saying that He meant only the idols by it and did not mean the prophets and the angels. But when Ibn al-Zibaʿrā saw that the words of the Messenger of Allah could, in their wording, bear a general sense, while he knew that what was meant was their idols and nothing else, he found a loophole for a trick, so he turned its meaning to inclusiveness and comprehensiveness by way of quibbling and obstinacy. The Messenger of Allah held himself in dignified restraint from answering him, until his Lord answered for him with His saying: «إن الذين سبقت لهم منّا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون» ("Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it"), thereby showing that the verse is specific to the idols. This is the gist of the story. It must be noted that ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā was a well-known Companion and a famous poet; he accepted Islam and his Islam was good, and this story, supposing it sound, was before his conversion. Al-Zibaʿrā, with kasra on the zāy, fatḥa on the bāʾ, sukūn on the ʿayn and a fatḥa on the rāʾ with a short alif, means in the language "the ill-natured".

dervis-irab:63-65.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا جاءَ عِيسى بِالْبَيِّناتِ قالَ: قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِالْحِكْمَةِ وَلِأُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain the intransigence of the Children of Israel. لما is a connective or temporal; جاء عيسى is a past verb and an agent; بالبينات are both attached to جاء; the clause قال has no grammatical position; and the clause قد جئتكم بالحكمة is the content of what was said. ولأبين: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of causation; أبين is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن, optionally so, after the lām of causation; and the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to بالحكمة. The wording of al-Shihāb: «His saying ولأبين لكم is attached to an implied element, that is, "and I have come to you in order to make clear"; the conjunction was not left out so that it might attach to what precedes it, to signal concern for the reason, so that it was made as though it were a speech by itself.» لكم are both attached to أبين; بعض الذي is a direct object of أبين; the clause تختلفون is a ṣila (relative clause); and فيه are both attached to تختلفون. (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ) You may take the fāʾ as a conjunction, so that the speech is conjoined to what precedes it as a completion of the speech of ʿĪsā, and you may take it as resumptive, so that the speech is a fresh speech from Allah, pointing to the way of obedience and its clear highway. اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; أطيعون is conjoined to فاتقوا, and the yāʾ, omitted to observe the writing of the codex, is a direct object. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ) The clause is an explanation of the preceding «وأطيعون»; إن with its noun; هو is a subject; ربي is the predicate; the clause is the predicate of inna; ربكم is conjoined to ربي; the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent inference (al-faṣīḥa); اعبدوه is a verb, an agent and a direct object; هذا is a subject; صراط is the predicate; and مستقيم is an adjective. (فَاخْتَلَفَ الْأَحْزابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; اختلف الأحزاب is a verb and an agent; and من بينهم is a ḥāl from الأحزاب. (فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ويل is a subject, and it has already been said that it is a word of punishment, and that is why it is permissible to begin with it; للذين is its predicate; and من عذاب يوم أليم is a second predicate or a ḥāl, that is, "being of the punishment of a painful day, the Day of Resurrection".

dervis-irab:9-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِقَدَرٍ) By a measure (bi-miqdār), that is, it provides what you need, so that it is neither too little to be of benefit nor too much so as to harm and injure.
(فَأَنْشَرْنا) We revived. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "nashara al-mawtā nushūran: they came to life; and Allah nashara them — the verb is both intransitive and transitive, and is also made transitive by the hamza, so one says anshara-hum Allāh. And nasharat al-arḍ nushūran also means the land came to life and put forth vegetation, and it is made transitive by the hamza, so one says ansharta-hā when you have revived it with water."
(مُقْرِنِينَ) Capable (muṭīqīn). One says aqrana al-shayʾ when he was able to bear it. Ibn Harma said:
وأقرنت ما حملتني ولقلما ... يطاق احتمال الصدّ يا دعد والهجر
(I have borne what you charged me with, though rarely is the endurance of rejection and desertion borne, O Daʿd.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The reality of aqranahu is that he found it his match (qarīnatahu) and what can be paired with him, because the difficult thing is not a match for the weak." Al-Akhfash and Abū ʿUbayda said: "muqrinīn means those who have control (ḍābiṭīn); it is also said, those who are equals in strength of hands and power, from their saying 'he is the qirn of so-and-so' when he is like him in strength. One says 'so-and-so is muqrin for so-and-so', that is, in control of him; and 'aqrantu such-and-such', that is, I was able to bear it; and 'aqrana lahu', that is, he was able to bear it and was strong against it, as if he had become a qirn (match) for it. Allah the Exalted said: «وما كنّا له مقرنين», that is, 'capable'." Others said: there are two views on its origin. One is that it is taken from al-aqrān; one says aqrana yuqrinu iqrānan when he was able, or aqrantu such-and-such when I was able to do it and mastered it, as if he put it in a qarn, which is a rope, and bound it and tied it with it. The second is that it is taken from muqārana (pairing), which is to tie some of them to others with a rope; you say qaranta this with that when you tied it to it and made it its companion.

* I'rab:
(وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ) The waw is a conjunction; the lām is the one that prepares for an oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); «إن» is conditional; «سألتهم» is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn because it is attached to a vowelled nominative pronoun; the tāʾ is the agent and the hāʾ is the direct object. (مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ) «من» is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the clause «خلق السموات والأرض» is the khabar; the interrogative clause is in the position of accusative as the second object of «سألتهم», whose operation is suspended (muʿallaqa) by the interrogative. (لَيَقُولُنَّ خَلَقَهُنَّ الْعَزِيزُ الْعَلِيمُ) The lām occurs in the answer of the oath because it is the one that came first, as the rule is; «يقولنّ» is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, which has been omitted because of the succession of like letters (tawālī al-amthāl), and parallels of it have already preceded; the omitted waw is the agent, and the nūn is for emphasis. Had it been jussive, the omission would be because of the jussive particle, not because of the succession of like letters. The clause «خلقهنّ» is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl); the verb is repeated for emphasis; «العزيز» is the agent and «العليم» an adjective. More on this verse will come in the section on Rhetoric. (الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْداً) The relative noun is a second adjective or a badal; the clause «جعل» is the ṣila (relative clause); «لكم» is attached to «جعل» if it means "created"; if it means "made into" (ṣayyara), then it is attached to an omitted ḥāl; «الأرض» is the first direct object and «مهدا» the second direct object, or a ḥāl. (وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ فِيها سُبُلًا) Conjoined to what precedes; «لكم» is attached to «جعل», or is in the position of the second object; «فيها» is a ḥāl and «سبلا» is a direct object. (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ) «لعل» and its noun, and the clause «تهتدون» is its khabar. (وَالَّذِي نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً بِقَدَرٍ) Conjoined to the first relative noun; the clause «نزل» is the ṣila; «من السماء» is attached to «نزل»; «ماء» is a direct object; «بقدر» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (فَأَنْشَرْنا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتاً كَذلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction and «أنشرنا» is conjoined to «نزل»; in it there is an iltifāt (shift of person), the secret of which will come in the section on Rhetoric. «به» is attached to «أنشرنا»; «بلدة» is a direct object; «ميتا» is an adjective of «بلدة»; «كذلك» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; «تخرجون» is verb and agent. (وَالَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَزْواجَ كُلَّها) Also conjoined; the clause «خلق الأزواج» is the ṣila; «كلها» is emphasis (tawkīd). (وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الْفُلْكِ وَالْأَنْعامِ ما تَرْكَبُونَ) Conjoined to «خلق الأزواج», falling within the scope of the ṣila; «لكم» is in the position of the second object; «من الفلك» is a ḥāl; «الأنعام» is conjoined to «الفلك»; «ما» is a relative noun, direct object; the clause «تركبون» is the ṣila and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "what you ride (tarkabūnahu)". A discussion of the verb "to ride" will come in the section on Benefits. (لِتَسْتَوُوا عَلى ظُهُورِهِ ثُمَّ تَذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ إِذَا اسْتَوَيْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ) The lām is causal and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «جعل»; «تستووا» is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām, and the waw is the agent; «على ظهوره» is attached to «تستووا»; «ثم» is a conjunction; «تذكروا» is conjoined to «تستووا»; «نعمة ربكم» is the object of «تذكروا»; «إذا» is a future adverbial attached to its omitted apodosis, which is indicated by «تذكروا»; the clause «استويتم» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; «عليه» is attached to «استويتم». The pronoun in «ظهوره» is singular in view of the wording of «ما», just as «الظهور» is plural for the same reason. (وَتَقُولُوا سُبْحانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنا هذا) «وتقولوا» is conjoined to what precedes; «سبحان» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; «الذي» is a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «سخر» is the ṣila; «لنا» is attached to «سخر»; «هذا» is a direct object. (وَما كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ) The waw is circumstantial (lil-ḥāl); «ما» is negative; kāna and its noun; «له» is attached to «مقرنين», and «مقرنين» is the khabar of «كنا». (وَإِنَّا إِلى رَبِّنا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ) The waw is also circumstantial (the secret of this ḥāl will come in the section on Rhetoric); «إن» and its noun; «إلى ربنا» is attached to «منقلبون»; the lām is the shifted lām; «منقلبون» is the khabar of «إن».

* Rhetoric:
These verses contain several kinds of rhetorical art, which we summarise as follows:
1- The first art in them is omission (ḥadhf). The thing described, namely Allah the Exalted, has been omitted and His attributes put in its place, because the speech is divided: part of it is their speech and part of it is the speech of Allah the Exalted. What is theirs is «خلقهنّ», and what comes after it is the speech of Allah the Exalted. The original of the speech is that they said "Allah created them", as indicated by His words in another verse: «ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولنّ الله». Then, when they said "Allah created them", Allah the Exalted described Himself with these attributes, and they were put in the place of the thing described, as though it were a single speech. A parallel to this is that you say to a man: "Who of the people honoured you?" and he says: "Zayd honoured me," and you, describing him, say: "The generous, the munificent, the bountiful, he whose attribute is such and such."
2- Iltifāt (shift): the second art is iltifāt. When the transition took place from their speech to the speech of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, its beginning came in the form of the third person, and its end shifted from it to the first person in His words «فأنشرنا», as a display of artistry among the arts of rhetoric, and to record His favour upon His servants and strike their ears with it. Examples of this kind in the Qur'an are many.
3- The secret of the ḥāl: the secret in His words «وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون» is that many a rider's mount has stumbled with him, or bolted, or he has fallen from its back and perished, and many a pair of passengers in a ship have had it break up with them and drowned. Since riding in itself is a hard matter, because of the danger whose outcome is unknown, and the rider is exposed to all kinds of destruction and sorts of peril, it is his right not to forget that he is bound to perish and that he will return to Allah, and that he will not be able to escape His decree when it is decided, nor His ordainment when it descends. The aim of all that is that he be attentive to himself and not prefer his worldly life over his Hereafter.

* Benefits:
Among the secrets that are subtle to understanding are the topics of the transitivity of verbs. The Arabs make one verb transitive sometimes by itself and sometimes by means of an intermediary, like sakartu (I shut/I was intoxicated) and its sisters; and they make synonymous verbs transitive by different instruments, such as daʿawtu and ṣallaytu: you say "the Prophet invoked blessing upon the family of Abū Awfā (ṣallā ʿalā āl Abī Awfā)", but if you said "daʿā ʿalā āl Abī Awfā" it would convey the opposite of the intended meaning; rather one says "daʿā li-āl Abī Awfā". They also make one of two verbs transitive to two objects and its synonym to one object, like ʿalima and ʿarafa, so that the difference in transitivity and intransitivity does not entail a difference in meaning. It follows from this that "rakiba", according to both categories, has a single meaning, even if one of them is particular to the presence of the intermediary and the other to its absence. So the correct view is one of two things. Either the two connected elements are assumed as they would be if each stood alone, so that the implied form would be "what you ride (tarkabūnahu) and what you ride on (tarkabūna fīhi)"; or, closer, it is explained by considering it as transitive by itself, and this would be a case of giving precedence to one of the two aspects of the verb over the other, which is easier than the giving of precedence in His words «فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم» on one of the two interpretations of it, because there the difference between the two verbs is firm in meaning (I mean gathering the matter and gathering the partners), but when they came close, one prevailed over the other, and then the prevailing one was made the one that is transitive by itself. [Translator's note: this passage is obscure in the source; it is rendered as literally as possible.]

dervis-irab:15-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جُزْءاً) He said in al-Qāmūs: "Al-juzʾ: a part (baʿḍ), and it may be vowelled with fatḥa; the plural is ajzāʾ; with ḍamma it is a place and a sand-dune. Jazaʾahu, like jaʿalahu, means he divided it into parts, like jazzaʾahu; and bi-l-shayʾ means he was content with it, like ijtazaʾa and tajazzaʾa; and al-shayʾ means he tightened it; and the camels ... with fresh pasture instead of water: they were satisfied, like jazaʾat with kasra; I made them content (ajzaʾtuhā) and I portioned them (jazzaʾtuhā); and ajzaʾtu ʿanka majzaʾa fulān and majzaʾatahu, which can also be read with ḍamma: I sufficed in your place as he would have sufficed; and the awl: I made for it a juzʾa, that is, a handle; and the ring on my finger: I put it on; and the pasture: its vegetation became dense; and the mother: she bore females; and a sheep on your behalf: it sufficed, a dialect form of jazat; and al-shayʾ iyyāya: it sufficed me; and al-jawāzi' are the wild animals. «وجعلوا له من عباده جزءا», that is, females." Al-Zamakhsharī rejected this and said it is a contrivance, not language. The text of his statement follows: "The meaning of «من عباده جزءا» is that they said: the angels are the daughters of Allah, so they made them a part of Him and a portion of Him, as a child is a piece of his father and a part of him. Among the novelties of exegesis is the interpretation of juzʾ as females and the claim that juzʾ in the language of the Arabs is a name for females; it is nothing but a lie against the Arabs and a newly invented and altered usage. That did not satisfy them until they derived from it ajzaʾat al-marʾa, and then fabricated a verse:
إن أجزأت حرة يوما فلا عجب ... زوجتها من بنات الأوس مجزئة
(If a free woman bears a female one day, do not be surprised: I married her to a woman of the daughters of al-Aws who bears females.)"
Al-Zamakhsharī may have an excuse for finding this interpretation implausible, but his excuse vanishes when we recall that al-Zajjāj and al-Mubarrad are the ones who reported it, and they are two imams of the Arabic language and its guardians, to whom the final word in knowing it belongs.
(الْحِلْيَةِ) Adornment.

* I'rab:
(وَجَعَلُوا لَهُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ جُزْءاً) The waw is a conjunction according to al-Zamakhsharī, because he made the speech connected to His words «ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض», i.e. "and yet, despite that admission, they made a part of His servants for Him, describing Him with the attributes of the created"; but you may make it resumptive. «جعلوا» is verb and agent; making here means "making into" (taṣyīr); «له» is in the position of the second object; «من عباده» is a ḥāl; «جزءا» is the first object of «جعلوا». (إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَكَفُورٌ مُبِينٌ) «إن» and its noun; the shifted lām; «كفور» is the khabar of «إن»; «مبين» is an adjective, i.e. one who makes his ingratitude manifest. (أَمِ اتَّخَذَ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ بَناتٍ وَأَصْفاكُمْ بِالْبَنِينَ) «أم» is the connected (muttaṣila) type, conjoined to an omitted interrogative whose purpose is denial and rebuke, the implied form being "Do you say …, or has He taken…?". Some said it is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) type meaning "rather" (bal), and others said it is both; each is sound, and «أم» has already been discussed at length. «اتخذ» is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He" (هو); «مما» is attached to an omitted element which is the second object of «اتخذ»; the clause «يخلق» is the ṣila; «بنات» is the first object of «اتخذ»; «أصفاكم» is conjoined to «اتخذ»; «بالبنين» is attached to «أصفاكم». (وَإِذا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِما ضَرَبَ لِلرَّحْمنِ مَثَلًا) The waw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, introduced to confirm what precedes; «إذا» is a future adverbial containing the meaning of condition; «بشّر» is a passive past verb; «أحدهم» is the deputy agent; «بما» is attached to «بشر»; the clause «ضرب» is the ṣila; «ضرب» contains the meaning of "made" (jaʿala), so «للرحمن» is attached to an omitted element in the position of the second object; «مثلا» is the first object of «ضرب». (ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ) «ظل» is a defective past verb, «وجهه» its noun and «مسودّا» its khabar; the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the waw is circumstantial; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «كظيم» its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. (أَوَمَنْ يُنَشَّؤُا فِي الْحِلْيَةِ وَهُوَ فِي الْخِصامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ) The hamza is for rhetorical (disapproving) interrogation; the waw is a conjunction, joining the clause to an implied clause, i.e. "They dare, and reach the furthest limits in bad manners, and assign to Allah one who is raised amid adornment". «من» is a relative noun, direct object of an omitted verb; it has been said that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "a part and a child". The clause «ينشّؤ» is the ṣila; «ينشّؤ» is passive, and the deputy agent is a latent pronoun referring to «من»; «في الحلية» is attached to «ينشّؤ»; «في الخصام» is attached to «مبين»; «غير مبين» is the khabar of «هو», and the clause is a ḥāl. The words of Abu al-Baqāʾ: "If you say: the muḍāf ilayhi does not operate on what precedes (the muḍāf), it is said: except in the case of «غير», because it contains the meaning of negation, as if He had said: 'and he does not make himself clear in disputation'. Similar to it is the problem in al-Kitāb: 'anā zaydan ghayru ḍārib'. It is also said that it is accusative by a verb which ḍārib explains, and likewise in the verse." It has also been said that it belongs to the category of «على لا حب لا يهتدي بناره», i.e. there is no beacon to be guided by; that is, there is no disputation from them; and this is not far-fetched. (وَجَعَلُوا الْمَلائِكَةَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ عِبادُ الرَّحْمنِ إِناثاً) The waw is a conjunction; «جعلوا» is verb and agent; «الملائكة» is the first object of «جعلوا»; «الذين» is an adjective; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and «عباد الرحمن» its khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of «الذين»; «إناثا» is the second object of «جعلوا». (أَشَهِدُوا خَلْقَهُمْ سَتُكْتَبُ شَهادَتُهُمْ وَيُسْئَلُونَ) The sīn is a particle of futurity (its secret will come in the section on Rhetoric); «تكتب» is a passive imperfect verb; «شهادتهم» is the deputy agent; «يسألون» is conjoined to «ستكتب».

* Rhetoric:
The meaning of futurity: He only turned toward the future, bringing the sīn that indicates it, so that the speech would contain the meaning of ample time for repentance, and so as to build hope on appealing for its acceptance before what they said is recorded; in keeping with what they believed about preferring males over females and ascribing the worse of the two parts, namely females, to Allah. In this is the utmost declaration of foolishness of their opinions, for they wronged our second half by ascribing evil and deficiency of intellect to it, then wronged their Creator by ascribing this part, which is evil, to Him. It is related of one of the Arabs that his wife gave birth to a girl, so he abandoned the house in which the woman was, and she said:
ما لأبي حمزة لا يأتينا ... يظل في البيت الذي يلينا
غضبان أن لا نلد البنينا ... ليس لنا من أمرنا ماشينا
وإنما نأخذ ما أعطينا ... حكمة ربي ذي الجلال فينا
(What is wrong with Abū Ḥamza that he does not come to us, but stays in the house next to ours, angry that we do not bear sons? We have no say in our affair as we wish; we only take what we are given, the wisdom of my Lord, Possessor of Majesty, concerning us.)

dervis-irab:66-73.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَخِلَّاءُ) The plural of khalīl, which is "friend". In al-Miṣbāḥ: «The khalīl is the friend, and the plural is akhillāʾ, like aṣdiqāʾ». And in al-Qāmūs: «And khill, with kasra or ḍamma, is the special friend, and it is only used with affection; one says "he was a beloved friend (wudd and khill) to me", and the plural is akhlāl, like khalīl, and the plural of this is akhillāʾ and khillān; or the khalīl is the truthful one, or one of the purest and soundest affection.» Al-Tāj added: «Ibn Sīda said: the kasra on the khāʾ is more frequent, and a woman too is called khill.»
(تُحْبَرُونَ) You will be made glad with a gladness whose ḥibār, that is, its trace, shows on your faces. Al-Zajjāj said: you will be honoured with an honouring carried to extremes; and ḥabra is exaggeration in what is described as beautiful. In al-Qāmūs: «And al-ḥabr, with two fatḥas, is the trace, like al-ḥibār, with kasra or fatḥa on its first letter.»
(بِصِحافٍ) With large dishes. Al-Kisāʾī said: «The largest of the dishes is the jafna, then the qaṣʿa, which satisfies ten, then the ṣaḥfa, which satisfies five, then the mi'kala, which satisfies two or three.»
(وَأَكْوابٍ) The plural of kūb, which is a vessel with no handle. Quṭrub said: the pitcher (ibrīq) has no handle. Al-Akhfash said: the ibrīq has no spout. It is also said that it is like the ibrīq except that it has no ear or grip. Abū Manṣūr al-Jawālīqī said: «It is without a handle only so that the drinker may drink from whichever side he wishes, because a handle turns the drinker away from some sides.» ʿAdī said:
متكئا تصفق أبوابه ... يسعى عليه العبد بالكوب
(Reclining, with his doors clapping; the servant runs to him with the cup.)

* I'rab:
(هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ) هل is a particle of interrogation whose meaning is negation, that is, "they await nothing"; ينظرون is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; الساعة is a direct object; and أن تأتيهم: the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and تأتيهم is a badal (substitute) for الساعة, a substitute of inclusion, the meaning being "they await only the coming of the Hour". بغتة is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl; هم is a subject (mubtadaʾ); the clause لا يشعرون is the predicate; and the clause is a second ḥāl. (الْأَخِلَّاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا الْمُتَّقِينَ) الأخلاء is a subject; يومئذ is an adverbial governed by عدو, that is, on that day every bond or friendship between friends will be severed and turn into enmity and loathing; إذ is an adverb annexed to its like, and the tanwīn is a substitute for a sentence, its implied form being "the day when the Hour comes upon them"; بعضهم is a second subject; لبعض are both attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, because in origin it was an adjective of عدو; عدو is the predicate of بعضهم; the nominal sentence is the predicate of الأخلاء; إلا is a particle of exception; and المتقين is the excepted by إلا, in the accusative. (يا عِبادِ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ وَلا أَنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ) The sentence is the content of an omitted saying, that is, "and it will be said to them"; يا is a vocative particle; عباد is the one addressed, a muḍāf to the omitted first-person yāʾ, in observance of the writing of the codex; لا is negative; خوف is a subject, and it is permissible to begin with it because a negation preceded it; عليكم is the predicate; اليوم is an adverbial attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl; the second لا is conjoined to what preceded; أنتم is a subject; and تحزنون is a verbal sentence in the position of the nominative as a predicate. (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِآياتِنا وَكانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ) الذين is an adjective of عبادي, because it is a muḍāf vocative; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; بآياتنا are both attached to آمنوا; وكانوا is kāna and its noun; مسلمين is its predicate; and the sentence is conjoined to the ṣila. Some preferred that the wāw be circumstantial and the sentence be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the wāw, and said that it is more emphatic. (ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ أَنْتُمْ وَأَزْواجُكُمْ تُحْبَرُونَ) ادخلوا is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; الجنة is a direct object by extension; أنتم is a subject; أزواجكم is conjoined to أنتم; and the clause تحبرون is the predicate of أنتم. (يُطافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِصِحافٍ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَأَكْوابٍ) يطاف is a passive imperfect verb; عليهم, in the position of the nominative, is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); بصحاف are both attached to يطاف; من ذهب is an adjective of صحاف; and أكواب is conjoined to صحاف. Gold is mentioned for the dishes, and this suffices without repeating it for the cups, as in His saying the Exalted «والذاكرون الله كثيرا والذاكرات». (وَفِيها ما تَشْتَهِيهِ الْأَنْفُسُ وَتَلَذُّ الْأَعْيُنُ وَأَنْتُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; فيها is a fronted predicate; ما is a relative noun, a postponed subject; the clause تشتهيه الأنفس is the ṣila of ما; تلذ الأعين is conjoined to the ṣila, falling within its scope; أنتم is a subject; فيها are both attached to خالدون; and خالدون is the predicate of أنتم. (وَتِلْكَ الْجَنَّةُ الَّتِي أُورِثْتُمُوها بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; تلك is a subject; الجنة is the predicate; التي is an adjective (naʿt) of الجنة; the clause أورثتموها is a ṣila; بما are both attached to أورثتموها; كنتم is kāna and its noun; and the clause تعملون is the predicate of كنتم. (لَكُمْ فِيها فاكِهَةٌ كَثِيرَةٌ مِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ)
لكم is a fronted predicate; فيها is a ḥāl; فاكهة is a postponed subject; كثيرة is an adjective; منها are both attached to تأكلون; and the clause تأكلون is in the accusative as an adjective of فاكهة. It is permissible to parse الجنة as a substitute for the demonstrative, in which case the sentence لكم فيها فاكهة is the predicate. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān, in agreement with that of al-Zamakhsharī, is: «وتلك الجنة is a subject and predicate, and التي أورثتموها is an adjective; or الجنة is an adjective and التي أورثتموها and بما كنتم تعملون is the predicate, and what is before it are two adjectives. If بما is the predicate, it is attached to an omitted element, and on the first two views it is attached to أورثتموها.»

* Rhetoric:
These verses are full of kinds of rhetoric and varieties of eloquence, which we summarise as follows:
1- Concision (al-ījāz): in Allah the Exalted's call to His servants. This call comprises four matters: 1- He negated fear for them; 2- He negated grief for them; 3- He commanded them to enter Paradise; 4- He gave them the glad tidings that joy would take possession of their souls.
2- Concision also: in His saying the Exalted «وفيها ما تشتهيه الأنفس وتلذ الأعين», for He confined the kinds of blessings, since they do not go beyond two things: either what the hearts desire or what the eyes delight in. It is related in the hadith that a man said, "O Messenger of Allah, are there horses in Paradise? For I love horses." He said: "If Allah admits you to Paradise, you will not wish to ride a mare of red ruby, which flies with you wherever you wish in Paradise, but you will do so." A Bedouin said, "O Messenger of Allah, are there camels in Paradise? For I love camels." He said: "O Bedouin, if Allah admits you to Paradise, you will find in it whatever your soul desires and your eye delights in."
3- Iltifāt (shift of address): in His saying «وتلك الجنة التي أورثتموها», for it shifted from the third person to the second for honour, the one addressed being each individual of those who enter Paradise; that is why the kāf is in the singular and He did not say «وتلكم», although what أورثتموها requires is that He say «وتلكم»; this is to signal that each one of the people of Paradise is intended for mention in himself.
4- Metaphor (istiʿāra): He likened Paradise to inherited wealth and abundant ancestral property, then borrowed the term "inheritance" for it by way of the implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya), because every deed must meet its recompense, since the deed departs and its recompense remains with the doer; or it was likened, in its remaining with its people and in the pouring out of complete blessings on them, to a lasting inheritance whose source never dries up and which never comes to exhaustion.
On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, a caller will call: 'You shall be healthy and never fall ill; you shall live and never die; you shall be young and never grow old; you shall enjoy comfort and never despair.' That is the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic «ونودوا أن تلكم الجنة أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون».'" Narrated by Muslim and al-Tirmidhī.

dervis-irab:74-78.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُفَتَّرُ) Is lightened. In al-Qāmūs: «فتر يفتر ويفتر fuṭūran and fatāran: it grew still after a time and grew soft after hardness; and fattarahu tafṭīran; and fatara al-māʾ: the water became still.»
(مُبْلِسُونَ) Silent with the silence of despair. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «ablasa al-rajul iblāsan: the man fell silent, and ablasa: he became still.»

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي عَذابِ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدُونَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to begin the threat after the abundant account of the promise. إن with its noun; في عذاب جهنم is a first predicate (khabar); and خالدون is a second predicate; you may also attach the preposition and its genitive noun to خالدون. (لا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ) The sentence is circumstantial; لا is negative; يفتر is a passive imperfect verb whose deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is latent, its implied form being "it", that is, the punishment; عنهم are both attached to يفتر; the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl; هم is a subject; فيه are both attached to مبلسون; مبلسون is their predicate; and the sentence is a second ḥāl. (وَما ظَلَمْناهُمْ وَلكِنْ كانُوا هُمُ الظَّالِمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; ظلمناهم is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; the wāw is circumstantial; لكن is the lightened, inoperative one; كان with its noun; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, or it is an emphasis (tawkīd) for the wāw; and الظالمين is the predicate of كانوا. (وَنادَوْا يا مالِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنا رَبُّكَ) The wāw is a conjunction; نادوا is a past verb and an agent; the past tense is used in place of the imperfect to signal the certainty of its occurrence, so it belongs to the type of «أتى أمر الله» ("the command of Allah has come"); يا مالك is a vocative (the discussion of Mālik and his being called will come in the section on benefits); the lām is the lām of command; يقض is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command; علينا are both attached to يقض, that is, "let Him cause us to die"; and ربك is the agent. (قالَ إِنَّكُمْ ماكِثُونَ) إن with its noun and predicate, in the position of the accusative as the content of what was said. (لَقَدْ جِئْناكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ لِلْحَقِّ كارِهُونَ) The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of affirmation; جئناكم is a verb and an agent; بالحق are both attached to جئناكم; the wāw is circumstantial; إن with its noun; للحق are both attached to كارهون; and كارهون is the predicate of inna.

* Benefits:
1- ʿAlī and Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them both, read يا مال, omitting the kāf, by tarkhīm (apocope). It was said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "Ibn Masʿūd read ونادوا يا مال", and he said: "How preoccupied the people of the Fire are, to be concerned with apocope!" And from one of them: what made apocope fitting for the people of the Fire is their weakness from completing the name, because they have no need of apocope. Ibn Jinnī said: «There is a secret in the apocope at this place, namely that, because of the greatness of what they are in, their voices grew faint, their strength weak and their souls abject, so this was a place for abbreviation by necessity.» Al-Ṭībī said: «I say: this is an excuse from him for the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, since Ibn ʿAbbās rejected it with his saying "How preoccupied the people of the Fire are with apocope!", for ما here is exclamatory, and in it is a sense of turning away, like your saying to someone in hardship who has busied himself away from it with what does not concern him: "What has so occupied you with this? Does what you are in of terror and hardship not keep you from this?"» I say: tarkhīm in the language is smoothing and softening; one says "a rakhīm voice", that is, smooth and soft; and in the technical sense it is the omission of part of a word in a specific manner, and it is of three kinds:
1- the apocope of the vocative; 2- the apocope of necessity (poetic licence); 3- the apocope of the diminutive; their discussions are in the books of grammar.
Mālik is the keeper of the Fire, that is, the chief of its guardians, whose command and whose seat are in effect over them, in the midst of the Fire, in which there are bridges that the angels of punishment cross; he sees its farthest part as he sees its nearest.
2- The hadith related to the verse: On the authority of Abū al-Dardāʾ, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hunger will be cast upon the people of the Fire, and it will equal what they are in of punishment, so they will cry for help and be given food of ḍarīʿ (thorny plant), which neither fattens nor avails against hunger. Then they will cry for help and be given food that chokes, and they will remember that they used to pass choking food down in the world with drink, so they will cry for help for drink, and it will be handed to them with iron hooks; when it comes near their faces it scorches their faces, and when it enters their bellies it cuts what is in their bellies. They will say: 'Call the keepers of Hell,' and they will say: «ألم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبيّنات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال». He said: Then they will say: 'Call Mālik,' and they will say: «يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك». He said: He will answer them: 'You are staying.'" Al-Aʿmash said: I was told that between their calling and Mālik's answering them is a thousand years. He said: "They will say: 'Call your Lord, for there is none better than your Lord,' and they will say: «ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنّا قوما ضالّين، ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنّا ظالمون». He said: He will answer them:
«اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون». He said: At that they despair of every good, and at that they begin the groaning, the regret and the wailing."
And on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The people of the Fire will call Mālik and he will not answer them for forty years; then he will say: 'You are staying.' Then they will call their Lord and say: «ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنّا ظالمون», and He will not answer them for a period like the world's lifetime; then He will say: «اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون». Then the people despair, and there is nothing but sighing and gasping; their voices resemble the voices of donkeys, beginning with gasping and ending with sighing."

dervis-irab:20-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَخْرُصُونَ) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "kharaṣa al-kāfir kharṣan, from the pattern of qatala: he lied, so he is a khāriṣ." And in al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: "al-kharrāṣ: the liar." The letters khāʾ and rāʾ as the first and second radicals of the word have a wonderful secret: they indicate abasement, filth, and the production of a bad effect. Thus: khariʾa khaʾan, kharāʾatan, khurūʾan: he defecated and had loose bowels. One says:
خرئت بينهم الضبع
that is, enmity entered among them. Al-mikhrāt and al-mikhraʾa: the place where one defecates; plural makhāriʾ. Kharaba al-bayt: the opposite of ʿamara (to be inhabited/built up). Kharaba al-rajul: the man became split-eared or pierced-eared, so he is akhrab and she is kharbāʾ. Kharbasha al-kitāb or al-ʿamal: he spoiled it; it is of the eloquent colloquial. Kharbaṣa also, meaning he took the money and went off with it, is likewise eloquent colloquial. Kharata al-udhun: he pierced the ear; and kharrata al-arḍ: he knew the land and its paths were not hidden from him, because he had gone through its regions and wandered in its sides. Al-kharthāʾ is among the attributes of the ugly woman: she is broad in the flanks and slack in flesh. Al-kharthī (with ḍamma on the khāʾ) is the worst of goods and their refuse, and kharthī al-kalām is what has no good in it. Kharaja: he emerged, which is well known. Al-kharrāj al-wallāj (with shadda) is one who goes out and in often. Al-kharāj (with the khāʾ vowelled in three ways) is tribute, and its origin is what comes out of the yield of the land and of wealth. Al-khurāj (with ḍamma on the khāʾ) is anything that comes out on the body, like an abscess. Al-khārijī is one who rebels against the ruler and the community, and from it the Khawārij were named, who are seven sects among the major Islamic sects. Kharkhara al-nāʾim: the sleeper snored. Al-kharīda is the pearl that has not been pierced. Al-khurūr (falling down) is well known, and there is abasement in it for the one who does it. Al-kharāza (cobbling) is a menial trade. Akhrasahu Allāh (Allah struck him dumb) is well known. "Feed the woman in childbed her kharsa" is her particular food, and she has been given kharas and so takharrasat. He said:
فلله عينا من رأى مثل مقبسي ... إذا النفساء أصبحت لم تخرّس
(By Allah, what eyes have seen the like of my fire-brand, when the woman in childbed has not been given her kharsa food.)
And "Allah struck him with a kharsāʾ", which is a calamity. Al-Akhṭal said:
وكم أنقذتني من جرور حبالكم ... وخرساء لو يرمى بها الفيل تلبّدا
(How often have you saved me from the dragging of your ropes, and from a kharsāʾ which, were an elephant struck with it, would cower down.)
Its original sense is the viper. ʿAntara said:
عليهم كل محكمة دلاص ... كأن قتيرها أعيان خرس
(Upon them is every well-wrought, smooth coat of mail, its rivet-heads like the eyes of vipers.)
And "I saw him wearing a shirt like the kharshāʾ of the snake", in thinness and clarity, which is its slough; and "he brings up from his chest foul kharāshī", which is phlegm and mucus. Kharaṭa al-waraq: he stripped the leaf from the tree by pulling at it. Wasamahu ʿalā al-khurṭūm: he humbled him; and "they are the kharāṭīm of the people" (their leaders); and "shurb al-khurṭūm" is safety, because it is the first that is pressed out. Al-Akhṭal said:
جادت بها من ذوات القار مترعة ... كلفاء ينحتّ عن خرطومها المدر
(She poured it for us, from the pitch-lined jars, full, dark-brown, the clay seal scraping away from its spout.)
In the stick there is khariʿ, that is softness and slackness, and from it the dissolute woman is called al-kharīʿ. He said:
يزيد جمال الدّل منها رزانة ... وحلم إذا خفّ النساء الخرائع
(Her coquetry's beauty is increased by her gravity and forbearance, when the loose women are light.)
It is limp like the castor-plant (khirwaʿ). Kharafa al-thimār: he gathered the fruit; "akhrifī lanā, O girl" (gather for us). Kharaqa al-thawb and kharraqahu: he widened its tear, and it became torn and ragged, and "the tear grew too large for the mender"; a kharqāʾ sheep is one whose ear is pierced; kharaqa fī ʿamalihi: he was clumsy in his work, and in him is khurq, and he is akhraq and she is kharqāʾ. Kharama al-shayʾ: he pierced it; and "ikhtaramahum al-dahr" and "takharramahum": time cut them down. Abū Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī said:
سبقوا هوى وأعنقوا لهواهم ... فتخرّموا ولكل جنب مصرع
(They outstripped my desire and hastened to their own; then they were cut down, and every side has its place of falling.)
And this is among the marvels of our noble language.
(أُمَّةٍ) A path (ṭarīqa) that is followed and aimed at; its hamza can also be read with kasra (imma).

* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا لَوْ شاءَ الرَّحْمنُ ما عَبَدْناهُمْ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain another kind of their disbelief. «قالوا» is verb and agent; «لو» is conditional; «شاء الرحمن» is verb and agent, and the direct object is omitted (its omission is frequent after the verb of will, as has already preceded), i.e. "had He willed that the angels not be worshipped, we would not have worshipped them"; «ما» is negative; «عبدناهم» is verb, agent and direct object; the clause has no position because it occurs as the apodosis of «لو». (ما لَهُمْ بِذلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ) «ما» is negative; «لهم» is a preposed khabar; «بذلك» is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective; «من» is a redundant preposition and «علم» is a postposed mubtadaʾ. You may also make «ما» a Ḥijāzī «mā», according to the view of those who allow the preposing of its khabar before its noun. «إن» is negative; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «يخرصون» is an imperfect verb in the nominative. (أَمْ آتَيْناهُمْ كِتاباً مِنْ قَبْلِهِ فَهُمْ بِهِ مُسْتَمْسِكُونَ) «أم» is a conjunction equivalent to the interrogative in His words «أشهدوا خلقهم», so it is the connected type. Some said «أم» is disconnected, meaning the hamza of rhetorical interrogation, as if, after denying their rational argument, He turned from the speech to deny their transmitted argument; al-Shihāb al-Khafājī preferred this view because it avoids the awkwardness with «شهدوا». (بَلْ قالُوا إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ) «بل» is a conjunction and particle of turning away (iḍrāb); «قالوا» is verb and agent; «إن» and its noun, and the clause «وجدنا آباءنا» is its khabar; the clause of «إن», its noun and its khabar is the quoted speech of their saying; «على أمة» is in the position of the second object of «وجدنا». (وَإِنَّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُهْتَدُونَ) The waw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun; «على آثارهم» is attached to «مهتدون» and «مهتدون» is its khabar. It has also been said that «على آثارهم» is the khabar, i.e. "walking", and «مهتدون» a second khabar, which is perhaps preferable.
