(وَكَذلِكَ ما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِنْ نَذِيرٍ) The waw is a conjunction; «كذلك» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and parallels of it have already preceded; «ما» is negative; «أرسلنا» is verb and agent; «من قبلك» is attached to «أرسلنا»; «في قرية» is attached to an omitted ḥāl; «من» is a redundant preposition and «نذير» is genitive in form and accusative in position as the direct object of «أرسلنا». (إِلَّا قالَ مُتْرَفُوها إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُقْتَدُونَ) «إلا» is a particle of restriction, and the exception is from the most general of circumstances; «قال مترفوها» is verb and agent, and the i'rab of what follows has preceded. (قالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْدى مِمَّا وَجَدْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ آباءَكُمْ) «قال» is a past verb and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو); the hamza is interrogative and the waw circumstantial; the implied form is "Will you follow your fathers even if I bring you what is better guided than that upon which you found your fathers of misguidance?"; «لو» is conditional; «جئتكم» is verb, agent and direct object; «بأهدى» is attached to «جئتكم» (the secret of the comparative will come in the section on Rhetoric); «مما» is attached to «أهدى»; the clause «وجدتم» is the ṣila; «عليه» is attached to «وجدتم». (قالُوا إِنَّا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كافِرُونَ) «قالوا» is verb and agent; «إن» and its noun; «بما» is attached to «كافرون»; the clause «أرسلتم» is the ṣila of the relative; «به» is attached to «أرسلتم»; «كافرون» is the khabar of «إنّا». (فَانْتَقَمْنا مِنْهُمْ فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; «انتقمنا» is verb and agent; «منهم» is attached to «انتقمنا»; «فانظر»: the fāʾ is a conjunction and «انظر» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); «كيف» is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, a preposed khabar of «كان»; «كان» is a defective past verb and «عاقبة المكذبين» is its postposed noun.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «قال أو لو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم قالوا إنّا بما أرسلتم به كافرون» there is the art of compulsion (al-iljāʾ), which is that the speaker takes his adversary by surprise with what compels him to admit the reality of his soul and the inner secret of his heart. The expression in the verse with the comparative, which implies that what their fathers were upon contained some guidance, was only to compel them to admit the reality of their intentions, which they hide, as though He descended with them to the furthest limits and gave them rein to the utmost extents, so that they would in the end confess their obstinacy, with which no counsel in speech avails, and in subduing which bringing proof is of no use.

dervis-irab:26-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَراءٌ) With fatḥa on the bāʾ, an alif, and a hamza after the rāʾ. It is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has taken the place of an adjective, and for that reason masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural are the same in it. In al-Mukhtār: "tabarraʾa min kadhā, so he is barāʾ min-hu, with fatḥa and elongation; it is not put in the dual or the plural because it is a maṣdar like samāʿ." In al-Qāmūs: "anā barāʾ minhu: it is not put in the dual or plural, nor made feminine; that is, barī'." 
(عَقِبِهِ) His offspring. In al-Qāmūs: "al-ʿaqib: running after running; and the child, and the child of the child, like al-ʿaqib on the pattern of katif."
(سُخْرِيًّا) With ḍamma on the sīn, relating to sukhra, which is work without pay. In al-Qāmūs: "sakhkharahu, like manaʿahu, sukhriyyan with kasra, and also with ḍamma: he charged him with what he did not want and overpowered him." Its explanation has already preceded. It is unlikely to be from sukhriyya in the sense of mockery and derision, contrary to the one who said it is from sukhriyya meaning mockery, i.e. so that the rich mocks the poor.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَراءٌ مِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ) The waw is resumptive and the speech is resumptive, introduced to remind the Arabs of the state of their remote forefather. The adverbial is attached to an omitted «اذكر» ("remember"); the clause «قال إبراهيم» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; «لأبيه» is attached to «قال»; «قومه» is conjoined to «أبيه»; the clause «إنني برآء» is in the position of accusative, the quoted speech; «مما» is attached to «براء»; the clause «تعبدون» is the ṣila of «ما». [Translator's note: the source writes «برآء» here in the quotation of the verse and «براء» in the vocabulary section; the verse itself reads «براء».] (إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ) «إلا» is a particle of exception and «الذي» is the excepted; the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), as if He had said "but the One Who created me, for He will guide me". It is also possible that the exception is connected, on the basis that they used to associate idols with Allah. Al-Zamakhsharī and others allowed «إلا» to be an adjective meaning «غير», on the basis that «ما» in «ما تعبدون» is descriptive (mawṣūfa), the implied form being "I am free of gods you worship other than the One Who created me", which is parallel to His words the Exalted «لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا». Abū Ḥayyān preferred a disconnected exception, since they did not worship Allah alongside their idols. [Translator's note: the source prints «يسركون»; «يشركون» ("associate") is meant.] The clause «فطرني» is the ṣila of the relative; the fāʾ is causal; «إن» and its noun, and the clause «سيهدين» is its khabar; the sīn is for emphasis, not for futurity, that is, "He will continue my guidance", since He the Exalted is his guide in the future and the present; the direct object is omitted, i.e. «سيهديني», to preserve the verse-ending (fāṣila). (وَجَعَلَها كَلِمَةً باقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ) The waw is a conjunction; «جعلها» is a verb, a latent agent pronoun and a first direct object, and the pronoun refers to Ibrāhīm; «كلمة» is the second direct object; «باقية» is an adjective; «في عقبه» is attached to «باقية»; «لعلهم»: «لعل» and its noun, and the clause «يرجعون» is its khabar. What is meant by "the abiding word" will come in the section on Benefits. (بَلْ مَتَّعْتُ هؤُلاءِ وَآباءَهُمْ حَتَّى جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ وَرَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ) «بل» is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb) and conjunction; the iḍrāb is from an omitted element which must be supposed for the speech to run on, the implied form being: "and he made it an abiding word among his descendants, by enjoining it upon them, hoping that the polytheists would return to it; but what he hoped did not come about; rather I gave these people, who are related to Ibrāhīm, enjoyment, and did not treat them with punishment, and I deferred their appointed terms." «هؤلاء» is a demonstrative, indeclinable on kasra, in the position of accusative as a direct object; «آباءهم» is conjoined to «هؤلاء» or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); «حتى» is a particle of end-point and of genitive; the secret of the end-point of the enjoyment will come in the section on Rhetoric. «جاءهم الحق» is a verb, a preposed direct object and a postposed agent; «رسول» is conjoined to «الحق»; «مبين» is an adjective of «رسول». (وَلَمَّا جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ وَإِنَّا بِهِ كافِرُونَ) The waw is a conjunction; «لما» is a connective or a temporal particle; «جاءهم الحق» is a verb, a preposed direct object and a postposed agent; the clause «قالوا» has no position because it occurs as the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ and «سحر» its khabar, and the clause is the quoted speech; «إنّا»: «إن» and its noun; «به» is attached to «كافرون», and «كافرون» is the khabar of «إنّا». (وَقالُوا لَوْلا نُزِّلَ هذَا الْقُرْآنُ عَلى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ) The waw is a conjunction on the preceding speech; «قالوا» is verb and agent; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning "why not" (hallā); «نزل» is a passive past verb; «هذا» is a demonstrative, deputy agent; «القرآن» is a badal; «على رجل» is attached to «نزل»; «من القريتين» is an adjective of «رجل»; «عظيم» is a second adjective of «رجل». More about the two will come in the section on Benefits. (أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ) The hamza is for rhetorical interrogation, charging them with ignorance and deeming their minds weak; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يقسمون» is the khabar; «رحمة ربك» is the object of «يقسمون». «رحمة ربك» is written in the muṣḥaf with the open tāʾ (tāʾ maftūḥa), the details of which will come in the section on Benefits. (نَحْنُ قَسَمْنا بَيْنَهُمْ مَعِيشَتَهُمْ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «قسمنا» is the khabar; «بينهم» is an adverbial attached to «قسمنا»; «معيشتهم» is a direct object; «في الحياة الدنيا» is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَرَفَعْنا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجاتٍ لِيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضاً سُخْرِيًّا) The waw is a conjunction; «رفعنا» is verb and agent; «بعضهم» is a direct object; «فوق بعض» is an adverbial attached to «رفعنا»; «درجات» is a tamyīz; the lām is causal, and it has been said that it is the lām of outcome (ṣayrūra or ʿāqiba); «يتخذ» is an imperfect verb, accusative by an optionally implied «أن» after the lām; «بعضهم» is the agent; «بعضا» is the first direct object and «سخريا» is the second direct object. What follows from this is what al-Khāzin set out when he said: "He means that if we had made them equal in all circumstances, no one would serve anyone, and none of them would be made to labour for another, and in that case it would lead to the ruin of the world and the corruption of the state of this life." (وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ) The waw is a conjunction or circumstantial; «رحمة ربك» is a mubtadaʾ and «خير» its khabar; «مما» is attached to «يجمعون»; the clause «يجمعون» is the ṣila of «ما».

* Rhetoric:
In the coming of the iḍrāb in His words the Exalted «بل متّعت هؤلاء» (the verse), and in making the end-point of the enjoyment the coming of the truth, there is a wonderful point. The aim of the iḍrāb is not to refute the preceding speech but to emphasise and continue, to show that they were preoccupied from the truth that had come to them, since there is no relation between the coming of the truth and the enjoyment. The meaning is that they were preoccupied from thanking the Bestower: instead of submitting to the truth, taking up its means, devoting themselves to it and seeking out its bounties, they brought something worse than the heedlessness they were in.

* Benefits:
1- What is meant by the abiding word among the descendants of Ibrāhīm, blessings of Allah be upon him, is the word of tawḥīd (divine oneness) which he spoke, namely his words: «إنني براء مما تعبدون إلا الذي فطرني».
2- What is meant by the two towns is Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif, and the two men are al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī in Mecca and ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī from al-Ṭāʾif, because the noble man with them, according to their silly beliefs, was the one who had much wealth and standing, and Muḥammad was not like that, so the message was not fitting for him.
3- The tāʾ is written open in His words «ورحمة ربك» in the muṣḥaf, as it is written in al-Aʿrāf, al-Rūm, Hūd and al-Baqara.

dervis-irab:79-89.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَبْرَمُوا) They made firm. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «abramtu al-ʿaqd ibrāman: I made the contract firm, and it became firm (inbarama); and abramtu al-shayʾ: I planned the thing.» One says abrama al-ḥabl when he has twisted it tightly, and what is meant is the second twisting; as for the first, it is called saḥl. In al-Qāmūs: al-saḥl is a cloth whose yarn is not twisted tight, like al-saḥīl. Zuhayr said, praising Harim ibn Sinān and al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf:
يمينا لنعم السيدان وجدتما ... على كل حال من سحيل ومبرم
(I swear, you two were found excellent chiefs in every condition, whether loosely or tightly twisted.)

* I'rab:
(أَمْ أَبْرَمُوا أَمْراً فَإِنَّا مُبْرِمُونَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to direct blame at the polytheists for what came from them. أم is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) with the meaning of بل, so بل is for rectification and for moving from the rebuke of the people of the Fire and the account of their state to the account of the offence of these polytheists; the hamza is for denial; أبرموا is a past verb and an agent; أمرا is a direct object; the fāʾ is a conjunction; and إن with its noun and predicate. (أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْواهُمْ؟) أم has been discussed already; يحسبون is an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is the agent; أن and what follows it fill the place of the two objects of تحسبون; the clause لا نسمع is the predicate of أنّا; سرهم is the object of نسمع; and نجواهم is conjoined to سرهم. (بَلى وَرُسُلُنا لَدَيْهِمْ يَكْتُبُونَ) بلى is a particle of response, that is, "We do hear that"; the wāw is circumstantial; رسلنا is a subject; لديهم is an adverbial attached to يكتبون; and the clause يكتبون is the predicate of رسلنا, and the sentence is circumstantial. (قُلْ إِنْ كانَ لِلرَّحْمنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْعابِدِينَ) قل is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you", and the sentence is resumptive, introduced to refute their claims, mentioned at the beginning of the sura, that Allah has a child from among the angels; إن is conditional; كان is a defective past verb; للرحمن is its fronted predicate; ولد is its postponed noun; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أنا is a subject; and أول العابدين is the predicate. The meaning of making worship depend on the existence of a child will come in the section on benefits. (سُبْحانَ رَبِّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ) سبحان is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; رب السموات والأرض is its muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement); رب العرش is a substitute (badal) for the first رب; عما are both attached to سبحان; and the clause يصفون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. (فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا وَيَلْعَبُوا حَتَّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent inference; ذرهم is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; يخوضوا is the answer to a request, and for that reason it is jussive; يلعبوا is conjoined to يخوضوا; حتى is a particle of limit and governing the genitive; يلاقوا is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after حتى, and the wāw is the agent; يومهم is a direct object; الذي is an adjective; the clause يوعدون is a ṣila; and يوعدون is a passive imperfect, the wāw being the deputy agent. (وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِي السَّماءِ إِلهٌ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ إِلهٌ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ) The wāw is resumptive; هو is a subject; الذي is its predicate; في السماء are both attached to إله, because it has the meaning "one who is worshipped". Al-Zamakhsharī gave as an example of it their saying "he is Ḥātim of Ṭayy, Ḥātim among Taghlib", on the implication of the meaning of "the generous one" for which he is famous, as if you said "he is generous in Ṭayy, generous among Taghlib". إله is the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "He", and the sentence is the ṣila of الذي; وفي الأرض إله is conjoined to His saying في السماء إله; هو is a subject; and الحكيم العليم are two predicates. (وَتَبارَكَ الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما) The wāw is a conjunction; تبارك is a past verb; الذي is its agent; له is a fronted predicate; ملك السموات is a postponed subject; the sentence is a ṣila; ما is conjoined to السموات والأرض; and the adverbial is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila. (وَعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; عنده is an adverbial attached to an omitted fronted predicate; علم الساعة is a postponed subject; إليه are both attached to ترجعون; and ترجعون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the deputy agent. (وَلا يَمْلِكُ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ الشَّفاعَةَ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; يملك is an imperfect verb; الذين is its agent; the clause يدعون is the ṣila of the relative noun; من دونه are both attached to يدعون; and الشفاعة is the object of يملك. (إِلَّا مَنْ شَهِدَ بِالْحَقِّ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ) إلا is a particle of restriction; من is excepted from الذين, and this is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); the meaning is: and their gods, meaning by them the idols and the images, do not possess intercession, as they claimed that they are their intercessors with Allah; but whoever bears witness to the truth, which is the oneness of Allah, and knows what he bears witness to, is the one who possesses intercession. The exception may be connected (muttaṣil), since the excepted-from would be omitted, as if He had said "and those whom they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession for anyone except for those who bear witness to the truth", so it is an exception from the omitted object, in line with the poet's saying:
نجا سالم والنفس منه بشدقه ... ولم ينج إلا جفن سيف ومئزر
(Sālim escaped with his life in his jaws, and nothing escaped but a sword-sheath and a loincloth.)
So it is an exception from those interceded for. The clause شهد بالحق is the ṣila of من; وهم: the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction; هم is a subject; and the clause يعلمون is the predicate. (وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the one that prepares for the oath; إن is conditional; سألتهم is a past verb, an agent and a direct object, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); من is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a subject; the clause خلقهم is the predicate of من; the interrogative clause, suspended, is in the position of the accusative as the second direct object of سألتهم; ليقولن: the lām is the answer to the oath, and the answer to the condition is omitted according to the well-known rule, namely when an oath and a condition coincide; يقولن is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, omitted because of the succession of similar letters, and the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; and الله is the agent of an omitted verb indicated by the relative of the interrogative, the implied form being "Allah created us", because the conditional proposition calls for neither occurrence nor non-occurrence. The evidence that the nominative is an agent of an omitted verb and not a subject is that it has come when there is no omission, as in His saying the Exalted mentioned above «ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن خلقهنّ العزيز العليم»; although this argument may be countered by a like one, so it is said: the evidence that it is a subject is that it has come like that, as in His saying the Exalted «قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر» up to His saying «قل الله ينجيكم منها». And what is said, that it was fronted to give the sense of specification, is disallowed, because the agent may not be fronted before its governor according to the sounder view. It is best to say that the verbal argument in this chapter is more frequent, so it is better to carry it over onto that. Ibn Hishām said: «Some of them say, regarding ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله, that the name of Allah, glory be to Him the Exalted, is a subject or an agent, that is, "Allah created them" or "Allah created them"; the correct view is to carry it on the second, on the evidence of ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولنّ خلقهنّ العزيز الحكيم.» Al-Damāmīnī, the commentator of al-Mughnī, followed him, saying: «This is contradicted by His saying the Exalted: قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر تدعونه, until he said: قل الله ينجيكم منها ومن كل كرب.» Al-Shumunnī followed him in turn, saying: «I say: it does not contradict it, because the discussion concerns only the particular answer whose basis is creation, not every answer.»
The fāʾ is a conjunction; أنى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف ("how"), in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and يؤفكون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the deputy agent. (وَقِيلِهِ يا رَبِّ إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) The wāw is for the oath; قيله, that is, his saying, is genitive by the wāw of the oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; and the answer is either omitted, that is, "I shall surely do to them what I wish", or mentioned, and it is His saying إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون, as if it were said "and I swear by his saying: O my Lord". It is also said that it is conjoined to الساعة, but that is far-fetched. It was read in the accusative. Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī said: «Its accusative is as a maṣdar (verbal noun) of its implied verb. It is said that the accusative is by conjunction to سرهم ونجواهم. It is said that it is by conjunction to the position of الساعة, as if it were said "He knows the Hour and his saying". It was read in the nominative as a subject, with what follows it as the predicate, or the predicate is omitted, its implied form being "and his saying is heard" or "accepted".» إن with its noun and predicate; and the clause لا يؤمنون is an adjective. (فَاصْفَحْ عَنْهُمْ وَقُلْ سَلامٌ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent inference; اصفح is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; عنهم are both attached to اصفح; قل is conjoined to فاصفح; سلام is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "the matter is peace"; the fāʾ in فسوف is a conjunction; سوف is a particle of postponement; يعلمون is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; and the direct object is omitted for magnification, that is, "the outcome of their affair".

* Benefits:
We promised you the discussion of making worship depend on the existence of a child. A long dispute has arisen among the exegetes and the theologians about it, especially between the Sunnis and the Muʿtazila. Al-Zamakhsharī said, in his brilliant style, the following: «قل إن كان للرحمن ولد: and if that is sound and established by a valid proof that you bring and a clear argument that you put forward, then I am the first to venerate that child and the first of you to obey and submit to him, just as a man venerates the king's son out of veneration for his father. This is speech that comes by way of supposition and illustration for a purpose, which is exaggeration in denying a child and elaborating on it, so that the speaker leaves no doubt except that it dissolves, while reporting of himself his firm footing in the matter of tawḥīd. That is because He made worship depend on the existence of a child, which is impossible in itself, so what depends on it is impossible like it. In the form of affirming existence and worship, it is in meaning a denial of both, in the most eloquent and strongest manner.» Then he put forward a mockery of the Sunnis and gave rein to his tongue, offending against the Divine Essence, when he said: «And its like is for the ʿadlī (Muʿtazilī) to say to the Jabrī (determinist): "If Allah is the creator of disbelief in hearts and punishes for it with everlasting punishment, then I am the first to say He is a devil and not a god." So the meaning of this speech, and what its style and composition were set for, is the denial that Allah the Exalted is the creator of disbelief, and His exaltedness and sanctification above that, but by way of exaggeration in it in the manner we mentioned, with a pointing to the ugliness of the doctrine and the error of the one who holds it, a decisive testimony of its impossibility, a declaration from himself of his disavowal of it, and the utmost aversion and repugnance at committing it.»
Abū Ḥayyān drew attention to al-Zamakhsharī's offence, saying after quoting what we quoted from al-Zamakhsharī's words: «Then he mentioned words for which he deserves discipline, even the sword; I have kept my book free of mentioning them.» This is not a refutation, as you see, but a meeting of abuse with abuse and of excess with excess.
Imam Nāṣir al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Munayyir al-Iskandarī al-Mālikī, judge of Alexandria, who died in the year 683 AH, replied to al-Zamakhsharī with a good reply, in which he followed the path of sound criticism. He said: «He has dared greatly and plunged into perdition in his illustration with the saying of the one he called an ʿadlī, "If Allah is the creator of disbelief in hearts and punishes for it, then I am the first of those who say He is a devil and not a god." Let such a person be requited for that by the saying of someone who says: it has been established by reason and by Revelation that He, the Exalted, is the creator of that in hearts as He created faith, in fulfilment of the requirement of the proof of reason indicating that there is no creator but Allah, and in affirmation of the content of His saying the Exalted «هل من خالق غير الله» and His saying «الله خالق كل شيء». If this premise is established by reason and by transmission, it follows that his ear should be rubbed and his neck shackled, for he deviates in matters of Allah with a deviation that none of His disbelieving servants preceded him in, and which no rebellious one of the wicked insurgents dared.» Up to the end of this reply, which was not free of abuse and insults either.
Then al-Zamakhsharī said: «People have strained in order to bring it out of this noble style, full of fine points and benefits that independently affirm tawḥīd in its most eloquent aspects. So it was said: "If the Merciful has a child, as you claim, then I am the first of the worshippers who affirm Allah's oneness and who deny their statement by ascribing a child to Him." And it was said: "If the Merciful has a child, I am the first of those who are disdainful (ānifīn) of His having a child", from ʿabida yaʿbadu when his nose swells (ashtadda anfuhu), so he is ʿabid and ʿābid.» And it was said: it is the negative إن, that is, "The Merciful has no child, and I am the first to say so, and to worship and affirm His oneness." Abū Ḥayyān refuted all these aspects at a length that the scope of this book cannot accommodate.
The wording of al-Shawkānī: «That is, if He has a child according to your statement and your claim, then I am the first to worship Allah alone, because whoever worships Allah alone has repelled the idea that He has a child. So said Ibn Qutayba. Al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī said: the meaning is "the Merciful has no child", and His saying فأنا أول العابدين is the beginning of a new statement. And it is said the meaning is:
"Say, O Muḥammad: if it is proved that Allah has a child, then I am the first to worship this child whose existence you claim, but it is impossible that He has a child." In it is a denial of a child in the most eloquent manner, the most complete expression and the finest style, and this is the apparent sense of the Qur'anic composition. Of this kind is His saying the Exalted: «وإنّا وإياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين»; and like this is a man's saying to one he is debating: "If what you say is proved by evidence, then I am the first to believe it and say it." So إن is conditional. This is what we chose, and Ibn Jarīr and others preferred it. There are other sayings that we passed over, because they belong to strained and artificial interpretation, and it is not fitting for the noble Qur'an to bring them or hint at them, since the Qur'an does not bring the rare or the anomalous of the language.»

dervis-irab:33-39.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سُقُفاً) In al-Qāmūs: "al-saqf of the house, like al-saqīf; the plural is suqūf, and also suqf with two ḍammas." From al-Farrāʾ: it is the plural of saqīfa. It has also been read «سقوفا» as a plural on the pattern fuʿūl, like kaʿb, kuʿūb.
(وَمَعارِجَ) Plural of miʿraj, with fatḥa or kasra on the mīm. The stairs by which one ascends are called maʿārij because walking on them is like the walking of the lame (aʿraj).
(وَزُخْرُفاً) Al-zukhruf is gold and adornment. Ibn Zayd said: it is what people keep in their houses of furnishings and furniture. Al-Ḥasan said: engravings; its origin is adornment. One says zakhrafat al-dār, that is, I adorned it, and tazakhrafa fulān, that is, he adorned himself. The lexicons give many meanings of al-zukhruf, among them gold, the beauty of a thing, and "zukhruf al-kalām" meaning its gilded falsehoods, and "zukhruf al-arḍ" meaning the colours of its plants; the plural is zakhārif.
(يَعْشُ) In al-Qāmūs: "al-ʿashā, shortened: poor sight at night and by day; and blindness is ʿashā like raḍiya and daʿā." And in al-Mukhtār: "ʿashā ʿanhu: he turned away from it; its pattern is that of ʿadā, and from it comes His words the Exalted «ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن»." I say: some interpreted it in the verse as weakness of sight. Abū al-Haytham and al-Azharī said: ʿashawtu ilā kadhā means I aimed at it, and ʿashawtu ʿan kadhā means I turned away from it, so a distinction is made between ilā and ʿan, like "iltu ilayhi" and "iltu ʿanhu".
(نُقَيِّضْ) We cause and we decree. One says qayyaḍa Allāhu lahu kadhā: He decreed it for him; and qayyaḍa Allāhu fulānan li-fulān: He brought him to him.

* I'rab:
(وَلَوْلا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً) The waw is resumptive; «لولا» is a particle of prevention due to existence; «أن» and what follows it, in the interpretation of a maṣdar, is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; «الناس» is the noun of «يكون»; «أمة» is its khabar; «واحدة» is an adjective. The meaning of their being one community is their agreeing upon one matter, and what is meant here is disbelief, by the indication of the apodosis, as will come. (لَجَعَلْنا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَمَعارِجَ عَلَيْها يَظْهَرُونَ) The lām is the connective of the apodosis; «جعلنا» is verb and agent; «لمن» is in the position of the second object; the clause «يكفر» is the ṣila of «من»; «بالرحمن» is attached to «يكفر»; «لبيوتهم» is a badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from «لمن يكفر» with the preposition repeated; «سقفا» is the first object of «جعلنا»; «من فضة» is an adjective of «سقفا»; «معارج» is conjoined to «سقفا»; «عليها» is attached to «يظهرون»; «يظهرون» is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the clause is an adjective of «معارج». (وَلِبُيُوتِهِمْ أَبْواباً وَسُرُراً عَلَيْها يَتَّكِؤُنَ) Conjoined to what precedes. The word «البيوت» is repeated for greater confirmation. You may also suppose an omitted verb to govern «أبوابا» and «سررا» in the accusative, so that it would be a conjunction of clauses. (وَزُخْرُفاً وَإِنْ كُلُّ ذلِكَ لَمَّا مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) «وزخرفا» is also conjoined to «سررا», or is a direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "and we made for them gold ornament". Al-Zamakhsharī conjoined it to the position of «من فضة», as if He had said "a roof of silver and gold", that is, some of them thus and some thus. The waw is a conjunction; «إن» is negative; «كل ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ; «لما» with shadda means «إلا»; «متاع الحياة الدنيا» is the khabar. It has also been read with «لما» lightened, in which case «إن» is the lightened form of the heavy «إن», without operation, the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and «ما» is redundant. (وَالْآخِرَةُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ) The waw is circumstantial; «الآخرة» is a mubtadaʾ; «عند ربك» is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; «للمتقين» is attached to an omitted element that is the khabar of «الآخرة». In this is a full confirmation that the truly great is the great in the Hereafter, not in this world. (وَمَنْ يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطاناً فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ) A resumptive speech, introduced to narrate the outcome of those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah. It has also been said that it is connected to His words at the beginning of the surah «أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا». «من» is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; «يعش» is the protasis; «عن ذكر الرحمن» is attached to «يعش»; «نقيض» is the apodosis; the two clauses of protasis and consequence are the khabar of «من»; «له» is attached to «نقيض»; «شيطانا» is the direct object of «نقيض»; the fāʾ is a conjunction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ; «له» is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «قرين» and was placed before it; «قرين» is the khabar. (وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ) The waw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun; the shifted lām; the clause «يصدّونهم» is the khabar of «إن»; «عن السبيل» is attached to «يصدّونهم». (وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ) The waw is circumstantial or a conjunction; «يحسبون» is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; «أن», its noun and its khabar stand in the place of the two objects of «يحسبون». The secret of the plural will come in the section on Rhetoric. (حَتَّى إِذا جاءَنا قالَ يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ) «حتى» is a particle of end-point and of genitive; «إذا» is an adverbial of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause «جاءنا» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; the agent of «جاءنا» refers to the one who turns away (al-ʿāshī) taken from the preceding «يعش»; the clause «قال» has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «يا» is a particle of alerting or of vocative, and the one addressed is omitted and apparent, the implied form being "O Lord"/"O you" [Translator's note: the source says only that the vocative is omitted and its implied form is apparent]; «ليت» is a particle of wishing and of accusative; «بيني» is an adverbial attached to an omitted preposed khabar of it; «بينك» is conjoined to «بيني»; «بعد المشرقين» is the postposed noun of «ليت». The meaning of «المشرقين» will come in the section on Rhetoric. (فَبِئْسَ الْقَرِينُ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; «بئس» is a past verb, not operating on the jussive, to form blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm); «القرين» is the agent of «بئس»; the specified object of blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "you" (أنت). (وَلَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ إِذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي الْعَذابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to set out what will be said to them in the Hereafter; «لن» is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; «ينفعكم» is an imperfect verb in the accusative by «لن»; «اليوم» is an adverbial attached to «ينفعكم»; «إذ» is an adverbial for past time, a badal from «اليوم». It is not to be said that «إذ» is for the past and «اليوم» for the present so the badal is not permissible, because this world and the Hereafter are connected and are equal in the judgement and knowledge of Allah, so that «إذ» is as if it were future and «اليوم» as if it were past. Ibn Jinnī said, in his questioning of Abū ʿAlī: "I went back to it several times, and the last that came from him was that this world and the Hereafter are connected, and they are equal in the judgement and knowledge of Allah." The clause «ظلمتم» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; «أن» and what follows it, in the interpretation of a maṣdar, is the agent of «ينفعكم», i.e. "your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you, as sharing in the calamities of this world benefits, where the afflicted one finds consolation in the like of his own". It has also been said that the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "your wishing" (تمنّيكم), which is indicated by His words «يا ليت بيني وبينه», i.e. "your wishing for distance will not benefit you". The reading «إنكم» with kasra supports the implied agent, since it is then resumptive and gives a causal meaning; as for the reading with fatḥa, «أن» and what follows it are in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "because you"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ينفعكم»; «في العذاب» is attached to «مشتركون»; «مشتركون» is the khabar of «إن».

* Rhetoric:
1- The indefinite noun occurring in the context of a condition: in His words «ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا» (the verse) there is a wonderful point, namely that an indefinite noun occurring in the context of a condition gives generality, and for that reason the pronoun refers back to it in the plural in His words «وإنهم ليصدّونهم»; the second is the waw in His words «ويحسبون» and the third is the hāʾ in His words «إنهم». [Translator's note: the source lists "the second" and "the third" but the first item is not stated in the text as printed; presumably the plural pronoun in «ليصدّونهم» is the first.]
Ibn Abī Ḥātim related, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Makhzūmī, that Quraysh said: "Assign to every man among the companions of Muḥammad a man who will seize him." So they assigned Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh to Abū Bakr, and he came to him while he was among the people, and Abū Bakr said: "To what do you call me?" He said: "I call you to the worship of al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā." Abū Bakr said: "And what is al-Lāt?" He said: "The sons of Allah." He said: "And what is al-ʿUzzā?" He said: "The daughters of Allah." Abū Bakr said: "Then who is their mother?" Ṭalḥa fell silent and did not answer him, and said to his companions: "Answer the man," but the people fell silent. Then Ṭalḥa said: "Rise, O Abū Bakr: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah." Then Allah sent down: «ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن» (the verse).
2- In this verse there is also the art of tankīt (the pointed choice), which is that the speaker aims at mentioning one thing rather than another that would fill its place, for the sake of a point in what is mentioned that favours its coming over anything else. Someone may ask: for what point did He depart from the literal word and not say "whoever turns away (yuʿriḍ) from the remembrance of the Merciful", and instead borrowed the word ʿashā (dim-sightedness) for misguidance? We say: the point is that the metaphorical word fulfils the intended meaning, unlike the literal word, for turning away is of two kinds: a turning away after which return is hoped, because the one turning away is able to return, and that is the turning away of the believer who holds the best belief, to whom there occur pleasures that absorb his thought and occupy his heart and mind with that pleasure, or its opposite, or other worldly matters, so he turns away from remembrance in that state; the companionship of Satan in that case is not permanent, because it is possible for him to return to Allah the Glorified and repent of it, and turn to the remembrance he had turned away from, whose way he knew of old and to whose path he was guided and in which he was brought up, or because of a divine solicitude required by an eternal precedent that draws him to it; and a turning away of misguidance from the path of right guidance and the way of good, such that even if we supposed that he wanted to turn to the good, the precedent of misguidance and wretchedness that has overcome him would prevent him. What is meant by turning away in the verse is the turning away of misguidance, not the turning away of heedlessness, so it is beyond doubt that the borrowing of ʿashā for misguidance is fitting in it. This is the turning-away one for whom the companionship of Satan is decreed wherever he is and wherever he may be; thus the place of the point is made clear that favoured the departure from the literal word to the metaphorical word.
3- Taghlīb (predominance): in His words «بعد المشرقين» is the art of taghlīb, which is common in their speech: they let one thing predominate over what belongs to another, by applying its name to the other and using the dual on this consideration, because of affinity and mixture between them. An example of taghlīb for affinity is their saying al-abawayn (the two fathers) for the father and the mother, and from it comes His words the Exalted «ولأبويه لكل واحد منهما السدس»; and al-mashriqayn (the two easts) and al-maghribayn (the two wests) and al-khāfiqayn (the two horizons), which is the place of khufūq, i.e. setting, from khafaqa al-najm, i.e. it set; and al-qamarayn (the two moons) for the sun and the moon. Abū al-Ṭayyib said:
نشرت ثلاث ذوائب من شعرها ... في ليلة فأرت ليالي أربعا
واستقبلت قمر السما بوجهها ... فأرتني القمرين في وقت معا
(She let loose three locks of her hair in one night, so she showed me four nights; and she faced the moon of the sky with her face, so she showed me the two moons at one time.)
that is, the sun, which is her face, and the moon of the sky. The two moons in common usage are the sun and the moon. It is also said that among such instances is al-Farazdaq's saying:
أخذنا بآفاق السماء عليكم ... لنا قمراها والنجوم الطوالع
(We have seized the horizons of the sky against you; ours are its two moons and the rising stars.)
and it has been said that he meant only Muḥammad and al-Khalīl (Ibrāhīm), peace and blessings be upon both, because his lineage relates to them. They also say al-ʿUmarayn for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; and it is said that what is meant are ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, in which case there is no taghlīb. As for the first, there is taghlīb in it: they let the lighter name predominate, and it is said, because of the length of his life. They also say al-ʿAjjājayn for Ruʾba and al-ʿAjjāj, and al-marwatayn for al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa. An example of taghlīb for mixture is His words the Exalted: «فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع», for the mixture is attained in the preceding generality in His words «كل دابة», which He then detailed afterwards, and in "those who walk on two legs" in the expression of the detail, for it includes human beings and birds. And His words the Exalted: «اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون», because «لعل» is attached to «خلقكم», not to «اعبدوا», lest it follow that a thing be explained by itself, i.e. "worship for the sake of piety (taqwā)", while taqwā is worship. They also let the masculine predominate over the feminine, so that she was counted among them in His words the Exalted: «وكانت من القانتين», that is, Maryam, and she was counted among the males, in that she was treated as one of them by the expression with a word that is specific to males in its original usage; and had there been no predominance He would have said «من القانتات».

* Benefits:
This world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever. In the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Tirmidhī: "From Abū Hurayra, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'This world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever.'" And from Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If this world weighed with Allah the wing of a gnat, He would not have given a disbeliever a drink of water from it."

dervis-irab:40-45.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفَأَنْتَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ أَوْ تَهْدِي الْعُمْيَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to console him ﷺ, i.e. these people are deaf, so you cannot make them hear, and blind, so you cannot guide them. The hamza is for rhetorical interrogation expressing astonishment; the fāʾ is a conjunction on an omitted element; «أنت» is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause «تسمع» is the khabar; «الصم» is a direct object; «أو» is a conjunction, and the clause «تهدي العمي» is conjoined to «تسمع الصم». (وَمَنْ كانَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) The waw is a conjunction; «من» is a relative noun conjoined to «العمي»; the clause «كان» is the ṣila of «من»; the noun of «كان» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو); «في ضلال» is the khabar of «كان»; «مبين» is an adjective. (فَإِمَّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإِنَّا مِنْهُمْ مُنْتَقِمُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional, its nūn assimilated into the redundant «ما»; «نذهبن» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis; «بك» is attached to «نذهبنّ»; «فإنّا»: the fāʾ is the connective of the apodosis, «إن» and its noun; «منهم» is attached to «منتقمون» and «منتقمون» is the khabar of «إن»; the clause «فإنّا» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (أَوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ الَّذِي وَعَدْناهُمْ فَإِنَّا عَلَيْهِمْ مُقْتَدِرُونَ) Conjoined to the preceding clause; «الذي» is the second object of «نرينك»; the clause «وعدناهم» is the ṣila; «إن», its noun and its khabar. (فَاسْتَمْسِكْ بِالَّذِي أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, i.e. "if you know this and are sure of it, then hold fast"; «استمسك» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); «بالذي» is attached to «استمسك»; the clause «أوحي إليك» is the ṣila. (إِنَّكَ عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is a justification for the command; «إن» and its noun; «على صراط» is its khabar; «مستقيم» is an adjective. (وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ وَسَوْفَ تُسْئَلُونَ) The waw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun; the shifted lām; «ذكر» is the khabar of «إن»; «لك» is attached to «ذكر» or is an adjective of it; «لقومك» is conjoined to «لك»; the waw is a conjunction; «سوف» is a particle of postponement (taswīf); «تسألون» is a passive imperfect verb and the waw is the deputy agent. (وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رُسُلِنا) The waw is a conjunction; «اسأل» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); «من» is a direct object; the clause «أرسلنا» is the ṣila of the relative; «من قبلك» is attached to «أرسلنا»; «من رسلنا» is a ḥāl. The discussion of figurative usage in this asking will come in the section on Rhetoric. (أَجَعَلْنا مِنْ دُونِ الرَّحْمنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ) The clause stands in the place of the two objects of «اسأل», whose operation is suspended by the interrogative; the hamza is interrogative; «جعلنا» is verb and agent; «من دون الرحمن» is the second object of «جعلنا»; «آلهة» is the first object of «جعلنا»; the clause «يعبدون» is an adjective of «آلهة»; «يعبدون» is a passive imperfect verb and the waw is the deputy agent.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage in the poets' questioning of abodes and traces: in His words «واسأل من أرسلنا من قبلك» there is a majāz mursal (loose figure), for the question has been directed at the messengers although what is meant is their communities, by the relation of guidance, which leads them to certain knowledge. Figuratively directed questions are frequent in Arabic where a question cannot truly be asked, and among them is poetry's questioning of dwellings, remains and ruins, as in the words of ʿAntara:
هلّا سألت الخيل يا ابنة مالك ... إن كنت جاهلة بما لم تعلمي
(Why did you not ask the horses, O daughter of Mālik, if you are ignorant of what you do not know?)
It has also been said that it is based on the omission of a muḍāf, so that it is a figure by omission (majāz bil-ḥadhf), i.e. "ask the communities of those We sent before you", and "why did you not ask the riders of the horses". This interpretation, and the intention of asking the communities, is supported by His words the Exalted «فاسأل الذين يقرءون الكتاب من قبلك».
